This is highly relevant to our work in LLM evolutionary search; adopting internal solver statistics as dense feedback signals rather than relying solely on end-to-end runtime fitness can drastically improve sample efficiency and search direction.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Tsinghua University, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore Management University

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: AsmEvo: Agentic Assembly-Level Optimization of AMD GPU Kernels with Functional Equivalence Verification
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: AsmEvo uses a long-horizon LLM agent to optimize compiled AMD GPU kernels at the assembly level, relying on the original binary as a differential oracle to verify functional equivalence before measuring performance. The paper presents strong empirical results on real hardware (MI308X/MI300X), achieving up to 3.88x speedups on KernelBench and 1.18x geometric-mean speedups on production vLLM/SGLang Triton kernels. The key insight is the strict separation between the LLM proposer and a deterministic, correctness-gated verification harness (using real-dispatch capture for a non-hackable fitness signal), which prevents the search from exploiting fast but incorrect programs. This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search and LLM serving optimization, as the architecture for verified composition and anti-stall memory can be directly adapted to improve the robustness and sample efficiency of our own agentic search frameworks.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD), Southern University of Science and Technology

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Eureka: Task-Conditioned Meta-Agent Orchestration for Scientific Discovery
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: ManXis introduces Eureka, a task-conditioned Meta-Agent architecture that dynamically compiles long-horizon tasks into obligation graphs and forms specialized Macro-Agents with tailored state, memory, and verifiers during execution. The results are backed by extensive empirical validation, including a 57.8% reduction in median context usage across 12,000 dependency-update tasks and successful application to open mathematical conjectures. The key insight is governed evolution: rather than continuously mutating the agent, the system uses a mathematically grounded cost-benefit threshold to trigger architecture evolution only when the expected amortized savings exceed the fixed cost of diagnosis and migration. This is highly relevant to LLM evolutionary search and multi-agent optimization, as it provides a rigorous, actionable framework for improving sample efficiency, managing persistent memory, and dynamically scaling agent architectures.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Duke University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Hokkaido University, South China Normal University, Guangdong University of Technology, ManXis

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Competing at Every Price Point with Agentic Evolution over a Menu of LLMs
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Borthwick introduces a cost-targeted evolutionary meta-agent that writes Python programs utilizing a menu of differently-priced LLMs to optimize the cost-accuracy Pareto frontier. The results are highly rigorous, Pareto-dominating nearly all baselines (including hand-engineered systems) on two AstaBench tasks using only 66 to 100 training examples. The key insight is that exposing a priced menu of LLMs to the evolutionary search and using a graded cost-penalty objective (pricing cost overages in error-equivalents) naturally forces the discovery of cheap-first cascades and selective strong-model escalation. This is essential reading for our work in LLM evolutionary search and multi-agent optimization, as it provides a concrete, proven mechanism for managing inference costs and sample efficiency during automated agent design.

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: GoalEvolve: From Handcrafted Algorithm Priors to Goal-Driven Evolution of Physical Design Algorithms
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: GoalEvolve is an LLM-based evolutionary search framework that optimizes physical design algorithms by targeting final full-flow metrics rather than stage-local objectives. The results are backed by strong empirical evidence, demonstrating a 30.67% improvement in total negative slack over default OpenROAD and outperforming standard Codex goal mode under matched evaluation budgets. The key insight is the use of 'effect-debt analysis' combined with an Evolutionary Program Database (EPD), which tracks whether a local algorithmic change causes downstream degradation and stores this as persistent mechanism memory to guide future LLM prompts. This is highly relevant to our research in LLM evolutionary search; the team can adapt the EPD and effect-debt tracking to improve sample efficiency and credit assignment in our own multi-stage optimization pipelines, such as routing or scheduling.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Fudan University

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Improving the matrix multiplication exponent with modern optimization and AlphaEvolve
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: This paper applies gradient-based optimization and AlphaEvolve to the combination loss analysis problem, improving the theoretical upper bound on the matrix multiplication exponent to ω < 2.371177. The results are rigorously verified using rational arithmetic, proving a genuine state-of-the-art advance over the previous 2.371339 bound. The key insight for LLM evolutionary search is the preparation pipeline: the authors relaxed discrete max-entropy constraints into a differentiable tensor program using the Sinkhorn-Knopp algorithm and Jax, enabling hardware parallelization up to 7 million parameters. They then applied AlphaEvolve using 'evolving constructions' to iteratively refine the optimizer while passing the best solution state between generations. This is highly relevant for our work, as it demonstrates how to successfully scale LLM-driven algorithm discovery for massive, highly constrained combinatorial problems.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Google DeepMind, MIT, Carnegie Mellon University, Columbia University

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: $\varepsilon$-MemEvo: Adaptive Cross-Task Memory Transfer for LLM Program Evolution
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: ε-MemEvo introduces a cross-task memory framework for LLM program evolution that stores natural-language strategy summaries from prior tasks and uses a contextual Thompson Sampling gate to control their injection into new tasks. The results are rigorously backed by empirical data, demonstrating an 8.7% improvement in convergence area (AUCC) and a 9.4% boost in early-stage convergence across 8 optimization benchmarks using GPT-5. The key insight is that cross-task memory transfer in evolutionary coding is fundamentally a safety problem; naive memory injection causes catastrophic negative transfer, but an adaptive bandit gate successfully suppresses mismatched tactics while retaining the benefits of aligned ones. This is exceptionally relevant to our research in LLM evolutionary search, providing a concrete, low-overhead mechanism to safely reuse algorithmic discoveries across different optimization domains without sacrificing search stability.

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: MEGA: Self-Evolving Agent Optimization Infrastructure via Wisdom Graph
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: MEGA is a three-layer infrastructure for self-evolving agent optimization that distills execution traces into a structured 'Wisdom Graph' and uses a multi-agent loop to iteratively improve agent workflows. The results are backed by strong empirical numbers, achieving a 76.55 aggregate score on four benchmarks (HotpotQA, IFBench, HoVer, PUPA) and outperforming SOTA optimizers like GEPA and TextGrad. The key insight is the 'Seed-Epoch' evaluation regime—which fixes the evaluation seed during an optimization epoch to eliminate data variance and isolate the true impact of strategy changes—alongside the decomposition of memory into atomic Primary-Context-Resultant (PCR) triplets for logical reasoning. This is highly relevant to our work in LLM evolutionary search and multi-agent optimization, offering concrete architectural blueprints for persistent memory and reliable fitness attribution across search runs.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: megacode.ai

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Harnesses
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Zhou introduces Hierarchical Self-Improvement (HSI), a framework where a single frozen LLM evolves both its task-specific execution harness and the evolutionary search strategy used to improve that harness. The results are backed by strong empirical evidence on the BALROG benchmark, showing massive gains (e.g., +39.3% on BabyAI, +33.0% on Crafter) using DeepSeek-V4-Flash, with ablation studies proving that evolving the search strategy itself contributes significantly to the performance. The key insight is the three-layer hierarchical architecture (task harness, evolver, meta-evolver) bounded by a frozen outer anchor, which allows the system to safely rewrite its own seed selection and commit policies without unbounded self-reference. This is highly relevant to our work in LLM evolutionary search, as it provides a concrete, implementable blueprint for 'evolving the evolver' to improve search efficiency and discovery quality.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: HKUST

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: PACE: Primitive-Aware Code Evolution for Automated Algorithm Design
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Xie et al. introduce Primitive-Aware Code Evolution (PACE), which improves LLM-based automated algorithm design by extracting and preserving useful local logic as reusable Executable Algorithmic Primitives (EAPs). The method demonstrates strong empirical results, outperforming recent baselines like ReEvo and MCTS-AHD on zero-shot transfer for TSP (e.g., achieving a cost of 28.13 vs 50.29 on 1000-node TSP-ACO) and continuous control tasks. The key insight is using Thompson Sampling to evaluate the parent-relative performance improvement of individual EAPs, effectively solving the credit assignment problem for sub-components without requiring extra evaluation budgets. This is highly relevant to our work in LLM evolutionary search, as it provides a concrete, implementable architecture for persistent memory and modular code generation that directly improves search efficiency.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen University

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Relay, Don't Route: Adaptive Population Handoff for Cost-Efficient LLM-Driven Evolution
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: RelayEvolve is a training-free framework that reduces the cost of LLM-driven evolutionary search by using a cheap model to explore and curate a quality-diverse population, which is then handed off to a strong model for refinement. The results are backed by solid empirical evidence, showing it outperforms single-model and call-level routing baselines in 11 of 12 budget-benchmark settings across four program evolution tasks. The key insight is that because evolutionary search is stateful, budget allocation should focus on population handoff rather than individual mutation steps; cheap models can efficiently capture front-loaded progress to build a diverse seed bank. This is highly relevant for our research in LLM evolutionary search, offering a concrete, implementable strategy to drastically reduce API costs while maintaining or improving search quality.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Carnegie Mellon University, The University of Hong Kong, City University of Hong Kong, JIUTIAN Research, China Mobile

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: MuEvo: LLM-Driven Evolution of Multi-Heuristic Ensemble
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: MuEvo introduces an LLM-driven co-evolutionary framework that simultaneously optimizes multiple interacting heuristics within an algorithmic solver (like ACO or Selection Hyper-Heuristics) rather than isolating a single component. The results are backed by extensive numerical evidence across TSP, CVRP, BPP, and Flowshop, showing consistent improvements over human-designed defaults and single-component LLM-AHD baselines (e.g., reducing the TSP-L optimality gap from 6.26% to 5.24%). KEY INSIGHT: To prevent a component from overfitting to a specific set of collaborators, candidate heuristics should be evaluated across multiple contexts (e.g., the current best ensemble, the initial ensemble, and a diverse secondary ensemble), while an LLM summarizes cross-component interaction history to guide joint pair evolution. This is highly relevant to our work in LLM evolutionary search; the multi-ensemble evaluation and dynamic component lifecycle directly address the co-adaptation challenges we face when evolving complex, multi-operator routing and scheduling solvers.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Southern University of Science and Technology, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: DGA$_2$D: Directed Graph-Guided Automated Algorithm Design with Large Language Models
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: DGA2D is an LLM-driven automated algorithm design framework that represents the search space as a directed graph, allowing simultaneous evolution of both the algorithmic pipeline structure and the underlying operator implementations. The results are rigorously backed by numbers across 12 combinatorial optimization problems (including routing and scheduling), showing a reduction in the optimality gap by up to 10.96 percentage points compared to state-of-the-art baselines like EoH and ReEvo. The KEY INSIGHT is the first-order path-dependent credit assignment mechanism, which evaluates the fitness of a specific code implementation based on its immediate topological context (the preceding operator) rather than just the end-to-end score. This is highly relevant to our work in LLM evolutionary search, as it provides a concrete architectural upgrade over fixed-template generation and directly solves the sparse reward problem in long algorithmic pipelines.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Beihang University

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: MOSAIC: Adversarial Co-evolution of Specialist Heuristics and Problem Instances for LLM-based Automated Heuristic Design
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: MOSAIC introduces an adversarial co-evolution framework for LLM-based automated heuristic design, simultaneously evolving problem instances and specialist heuristics within a Quality-Diversity (QD) grid archive. The results are rigorously backed by numbers, showing up to a 52% reduction in optimality gap on TSP and 33% on CVRP compared to state-of-the-art methods like ReEvo and EoH-S. The key insight is replacing global scalar feedback with contrastive multi-directional reflection: an LLM analyzes pairs of heuristics on adversarially generated instances, and a decision tree anchors these insights to specific feature-space regions in the QD archive to form a persistent, region-aware memory. This paper is highly significant for LLM evolutionary search, as it provides a concrete, implementable architecture for improving sample efficiency, memory, and fitness signaling when discovering algorithms for combinatorial optimization.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Georgia Institute of Technology

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: MOT-SR: Multi-Objective Tool-Augmented Scientific Equation Discovery with Large Language Models
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Wang et al. propose MOT-SR, an LLM-based evolutionary search framework for symbolic regression that uses a meta-strategy LLM to analyze data residuals with external tools and maintains a multi-objective Pareto front to guide equation generation. The results are rigorously backed by numbers, achieving state-of-the-art NMSE on 40 benchmark tasks and a 26.8x error reduction on a real-world astrophysics dataset compared to prior LLM-SR methods. The key insight is the 'Meta Strategy Generator' which autonomously invokes external analysis tools on the residuals of the current Pareto-optimal candidates to synthesize a natural language search strategy for the generator LLM, effectively acting as an automated planner for the evolutionary process. This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search; the dual-LLM strategy-generation loop and their AST-based structural diversity sampling could be directly adapted to improve sample efficiency and population diversity in automated heuristic design.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences, University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Goethe University Frankfurt

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Yang et al. introduce OpenMLE, a full-stack framework that post-trains an LLM via execution-grounded RL to act as the variation engine for long-horizon evolutionary search in machine learning engineering. The results are highly rigorous and backed by extensive numbers, showing their 35B model improving from a 39.4% to 71.2% medal rate on MLE-Bench Lite, surpassing GPT-5.5. The key insight is the meta-evolutionary loop: instead of using a frozen LLM, they explicitly train atomic operators (Draft, Improve, Debug, Crossover) using RL with adaptive bounds and entropic advantages, and deploy them in a search harness that uses multi-factor parent selection (quality, progress, novelty) and lazy, operator-conditioned memory synthesis. This is a must-read for LLM evolutionary search, as the structured experience cards and RL-infused operator training directly address the community's core challenges in sample efficiency, memory, and scalability.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Horizon Research, Frontis.AI, Tsinghua University, Zhejiang University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Georgia Institute of Technology

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: FunL2O: LLM-Guided Feature Function Design for Learning to Optimize
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: FunL2O uses an LLM in an evolutionary loop to automatically generate executable feature extraction code for Learning-to-Optimize (L2O) pipelines, replacing hand-crafted representations. Results are rigorously backed by numbers, showing consistent improvements across eight L2O baselines (e.g., reducing MILP solver wall time by 11-55% and LP objective gaps by 16-49%) while controlling for feature width and LLM sampling budgets. The key insight is the use of 'semantic feature contracts' to statically and dynamically validate LLM-generated tensor operations before triggering expensive model retraining, effectively constraining the search space. This is highly relevant to our work in LLM evolutionary search for operations research, demonstrating that evolving the state representation can be just as impactful as evolving the heuristic itself.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: IBM Research, University of Southern California, University of Wisconsin–Madison, Michigan State University

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: EvoPINN: Agentic Discovery of Executable Algorithms for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: EvoPINN is an LLM-driven evolutionary framework that autonomously discovers novel neural architectures and training programs for Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). Backed by rigorous empirical results, the framework evaluated only 56 candidates to discover algorithms that outperformed expert-designed baselines by up to 35% on complex PDE benchmarks. The key insight is its decoupled, module-wise evolution strategy: it uses a UCB scheduler to dynamically allocate LLM mutation budget between different algorithm components, combined with AST-based structural verification to filter out cosmetic LLM edits before triggering expensive evaluations. This is highly relevant for LLM evolutionary search research, as the telemetry-guided generation and modular credit assignment directly address the sample efficiency and sparse reward challenges inherent in automated heuristic discovery.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Budget-Aware LLM Discovery via Cost-Calibrated Frontier Utility
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: This paper introduces CostAda, an adaptive controller for LLM evolutionary search that allocates compute across search frontiers based on cost-calibrated utility (progress divided by realized token cost) and remaining budget. The results are rigorously backed by empirical evaluations across 8 benchmarks using GLM-5 and GPT-5.4, demonstrating that CostAda reaches the full-budget quality of state-of-the-art baselines (AdaEvolve, EvoX) using only half the token budget. The key insight is that progress-only credit is fundamentally flawed when search actions (e.g., short refinements vs. long-context guidance) have vastly different token costs; dividing fitness gains by the log of realized cost and shifting weight from local to global progress as the budget drains drastically improves search efficiency. This is highly relevant to our focus on sample efficiency and scalability in LLM evolutionary search, providing a concrete, implementable utility formulation to optimize massively parallel evolution runs and reduce compute costs.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI), City University of Hong Kong, International Digital Economy Academy (IDEA)

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: A Control System, a Dataset, and a Recipe for Making Frozen LLM Agents Learn a Domain
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: This paper formulates LLM agent harness optimization (prompts, tools, memory, planning) as a discrete control problem and evaluates online RL (bandits, REINFORCE) against a static DSPy-optimized baseline. Backed by rigorous empirical results across multiple domains and models, the authors find that online RL consistently underperforms the static DSPy baseline within practical episode budgets (e.g., 62% vs 96% success on tool-use). The key insight is that starting online controllers from a uniform prior over a discrete harness space is severely sample-inefficient; dynamic harness optimization must be bootstrapped from a metric-guided static optimizer to be viable. This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search and agent optimization, as it provides concrete evidence on the sample efficiency bottlenecks of dynamic harness tuning and offers a practical deployment recipe.

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: VPR-Evolve: Multi-Agent-Driven Algorithm Evolution for FPGA Place and Route
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Wu et al. introduce VPR-Evolve, a multi-agent LLM framework that specializes FPGA place-and-route algorithms by directly evolving the tool's source code for specific hardware designs. The results are backed by rigorous empirical evaluation on VTR-9 benchmarks, showing up to a 9.8% reduction in critical-path delay and outperforming Bayesian hyperparameter tuning with significantly fewer evaluations. The key insight is the framework's architecture, which uses staged evolution to optimize different algorithmic components sequentially and employs an 'Inspiration Collector' agent that injects new literature-based ideas specifically when the search plateaus. This is highly relevant for our research in LLM evolutionary search, as the multi-agent memory and plateau-recovery mechanisms can be directly adapted to improve search efficiency in our automated heuristic design pipelines.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Arizona State University

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: NeurGO: Learning to Generate Elite Candidates for Meta-Black-Box Expensive Optimization
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: NeurGO is a generative meta-black-box optimization framework that uses a Transformer encoder to capture population search trends and an MLP decoder to directly synthesize a small set of elite candidates for expensive optimization tasks. The method is backed by strong empirical results on CEC 2008 and COCO BBOB benchmarks (D=10), demonstrating faster convergence and better final performance than Bayesian Optimization and other MetaBBO baselines under a strict 300-evaluation budget. The key insight is that instead of generating raw candidate coordinates, the decoder outputs contribution weights used to recombine the existing population's representations, ensuring generated candidates remain anchored to known promising regions and avoiding out-of-distribution proposals. This architectural design is highly relevant for continuous latent-space optimization and could be directly adapted to improve sample efficiency when optimizing continuous representations of algorithms or heuristics.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: China University of Geosciences

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: SpecAHD: Localize to Specialize for Automated Heuristic Design in Large-Scale Routing Problems
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: SpecAHD introduces a bilevel LLM evolutionary search framework that co-evolves an upper-level program to expose local repair regions and a lower-level repertoire of specialized constructive heuristics to repair them. The results are rigorously backed by extensive empirical evidence, showing cost reductions of up to 57.7% against state-of-the-art AHD baselines (like EoH and ReEvo) on large-scale routing benchmarks including CVRP and VRPTW up to 10,000 nodes. The key insight is the 'Repair Response Archive'—a memory mechanism that logs heuristic performance on specific local structures during training, allowing a k-NN router to dynamically select the best specialized heuristic for new regions at inference time. This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search and large-scale routing, as it provides a concrete, scalable architecture for within-instance specialization and memory-augmented heuristic selection.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Guangdong University of Technology

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Teaching LLMs to Self-Evolve: Cultivating Core Meta-Skills with Reinforcement Learning
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Wu et al. introduce METAEVOLVE, a framework that uses reinforcement learning (GRPO) to explicitly train LLMs to perform iterative self-evolution and refinement. The results are rigorously backed by execution-based metrics, showing a 24% absolute improvement over AlphaEvolve on out-of-distribution coding tasks and a 46% relative speedup on open-ended algorithm optimization benchmarks. The key insight is that instead of relying on zero-shot prompting in an evolutionary loop, researchers can synthesize evolution trajectories (current code, fitness, history) from static datasets and use execution feedback as a verifiable reward to fine-tune the mutator LLM. This is a highly significant paper for our work in LLM evolutionary search, as it provides an actionable, scalable blueprint for RL-infused evolution that directly improves sample efficiency and search quality.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: From Monolithic to Modular: Segment-level Automatic Prompt Optimization
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: SAPO improves automatic prompt optimization by decomposing prompts into explicit segments (role, context, tasks, format) and applying targeted mutations only to weak segments identified via contrastive training examples. The results are backed by solid empirical evidence, showing a 5-7% average improvement over strong baselines like OPRO and EvoPrompt across five datasets (including GSM8K) using GPT-4o-mini. The key insight is the use of contrastive evidence (top-5 successes vs. bottom-5 failures) to explicitly classify components as 'strong' (to be frozen) or 'weak' (to be mutated), which prevents destructive interference during iterative search. This is highly relevant for LLM evolutionary search, as this segment-level diagnosis can be directly adapted to evolve specific sub-components of heuristic code or meta-prompts rather than relying on monolithic rewrites.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: ITMO University, AXXX

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Automated Discovery Has No Universally Superior Harness
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Gupta et al. systematically decompose and evaluate LLM-guided discovery harnesses across 3.1 million rollouts to show that no single fixed harness universally generalizes across models and problems. The results are highly rigorous, utilizing budget-matched statistical bootstrap tests to prove that complex evolutionary machinery often underperforms simpler tree-search or epsilon-greedy baselines. The key insight is that early search progress strongly predicts final performance, enabling an online adaptive allocation strategy that prunes weak partial runs and reallocates compute to surviving trajectories. This is a must-read for our work in LLM evolutionary search, as it dictates a shift away from engineering complex, fixed search harnesses toward implementing dynamic, early-stopping compute allocation to maximize sample efficiency.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: UC Berkeley, MIT, MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab, Weizmann Institute of Science

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Autonomous Discovery of Wireless Communications Algorithms
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Aït Aoudia et al. introduce AITE, an LLM-driven evolutionary search framework that uses a two-tier orchestrator-worker architecture with agentic tool-use to autonomously discover wireless communication algorithms. The framework produces real, empirically validated results, discovering an OTFS equalizer that is 3.6x faster than the state-of-the-art with better error rates, and the first explainable pilotless OFDM receiver matching neural network performance. The most transferable methodological insights are the post-processing adherence check (where an LLM verifies if the generated code actually implemented the assigned idea before updating the orchestrator's leaderboard) and the prompt refinement stage (which critiques worker execution journals to improve instructions for the next generation). This is highly relevant to our work in LLM evolutionary search; while the telecom application is outside our scope, the architectural enhancements for agentic code generation, adherence filtering, and prompt refinement directly address sample efficiency and search observability.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: NVIDIA

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Harness Engineering: Anatomy, Architecture, and Evolution of Coding Agents -- A Source-Code Study of Eleven Systems
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: This paper conducts a massive source-code analysis of 11 production LLM coding agents (including Claude Code, Codex, and OpenHands) to catalog their architectural patterns across loops, memory, tools, and multi-agent orchestration. The findings are backed by rigorous code audits rather than benchmark scores, revealing 29 recurring design patterns and two major 'absences' in production systems. The KEY INSIGHT is that production agents universally eschew heavy frameworks (e.g., LangChain, AutoGen) in favor of hand-rolled async loops, and rely on deterministic retrieval (ripgrep, ASTs) rather than vector-based RAG. This is highly relevant for our work in multi-agent optimization and LLM evolutionary search; adopting these production-grade architectural patterns—and dropping bloated frameworks—can significantly improve the scalability, debuggability, and reliability of our search scaffolds.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Inclusive Brains, Wavestone AI Lab

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Reward-Free Evolving Agents via Pairwise Validator
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Liu et al. replace the expensive scalar task reward in self-evolving agentic loops with a training-free pairwise LLM validator that compares parent and child candidates. The results are backed by rigorous empirical evaluations across prompt and code evolution engines, including ShinkaEvolve, demonstrating that this reward-free approach matches or exceeds full-reward baselines. The key insight is the 'Soft Elo' mechanism, which uses pairwise LLM verdicts to update candidate ratings for parent selection, entirely eliminating the need for scalar validation rewards. This is a must-read for our work in LLM evolutionary search, as it provides a highly actionable, drop-in replacement for costly reward engineering while maintaining search quality.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Accenture

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: How to Guide LLM Generation: Dual-Surrogate Guided Search for Automated Heuristic Design
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Wang et al. introduce Dual-Surrogate Guided Search (DGS) to improve sample efficiency in LLM-based automated heuristic design by learning which parent heuristics and mutation operators to select before querying the LLM. The results are backed by solid empirical evidence, showing superior performance over strong baselines like FunSearch and EoH across five combinatorial optimization tasks (including TSP and CVRP) within a strict 200-query budget. The key insight is the use of a transition surrogate that predicts the latent distribution of an ungenerated child heuristic based on the parent and operator, coupled with a utility surrogate to estimate its performance. This is highly relevant to our focus on LLM evolutionary search, as it provides a concrete, implementable mechanism to drastically reduce expensive LLM calls by shifting from post-generation filtering to pre-generation action selection.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Nankai University, South China Agricultural University

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: GAE: Graph-Augmented Evolution for Scientific Discovery via Reinforcement Optimization
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Chen et al. introduce Graph-Augmented Evolution (GAE), which enhances LLM-guided evolutionary search by integrating a GNN-based RL meta-controller for mutation selection and online GRPO fine-tuning for the LLM operator. The results are rigorously backed by empirical data, showing that GAE significantly outperforms static baselines like OpenEvolve and PACEvolve on symbolic regression benchmarks. The key insight is that replacing structurally blind, prompt-driven mutations with a learned policy (Discrete SAC) and continuously updating the LLM weights via group-relative rewards drastically improves sample efficiency and search trajectory. This is a critical read for our work in LLM evolutionary search, as the three-pillar architecture provides a concrete blueprint for implementing RL-infused evolution and overcoming the limitations of static LLM operators in heuristic discovery.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Georgia Institute of Technology, Shanghai Academy of AI for Science

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: QDEvo: A Multi-Objective Quality-Diversity Framework for Automated Heuristic Design
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: QDEvo integrates Quality-Diversity optimization into LLM-based heuristic generation by maintaining an archive of semantically diverse algorithms using pre-trained code embeddings and hierarchical reflection. Backed by strong empirical results, it outperforms the state-of-the-art MEoH baseline in Hypervolume and IGD across constructive routing, bin packing, and real-world scheduling tasks. The most actionable takeaway is using dense code embeddings to cluster generated heuristics and applying local Pareto competition within clusters, which effectively prevents the LLM from converging on homogeneous code structures. This is highly relevant for LLM evolutionary search, offering a concrete architectural improvement to maintain population diversity and improve exploration in automated algorithm design.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: George Mason University, Hanoi University of Science and Technology

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: MetaSkill-Evolve: Recursive Self-Improvement of LLM Agents via Two-Timescale Meta-Skill Evolution
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: MetaSkill-Evolve introduces a two-timescale framework where a multi-agent pipeline recursively evolves its own meta-skills (diagnosis, retrieval, allocation, proposal) alongside task-specific skills. The results are backed by solid empirical evidence, demonstrating up to an 8-point accuracy gain over fixed-operator evolution on QA benchmarks using a frozen 31B model. The key insight is that evolutionary operators can be parameterized as standard text files and optimized by the exact same pipeline used for task skills, guided by a 'meta-productivity' score that measures a branch's ability to generate strong descendants. This is a must-read for our work in LLM evolutionary search, providing a concrete architecture for 'evolving the evolver' and preventing search stagnation.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: LMU Munich, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, MCML, MemAgents Lab

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Harness-Aware Self-Evolving: Co-Evolving Model Weights, Harness, and Task Solutions
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: HASE introduces an agentic reinforcement learning framework that allows a single LLM to co-evolve its policy weights, task solutions, and surrounding harness (prompts, memory, evaluators) within a unified multi-turn action space. Backed by strong empirical results, an 8B model matches or outperforms 120B models on text classification and alpha factor mining, and matches AlphaEvolve state-of-the-art on circle packing while successfully repairing an initially broken evaluator. The key insight is the divergence-driven evaluator repair mechanism, where the model edits the local evaluator only when its proxy score diverges from a sparse real-world oracle score, providing a safe way to fix flawed reward signals without unconstrained reward hacking. This is highly relevant for LLM evolutionary search and automated algorithm design, as it provides a concrete methodology for evolving the search pipeline itself and improving sample efficiency through dynamic harness optimization and RL-infused evolution.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: The University of Hong Kong, China Mobile, Jiutian Research, Grace Investment Machine

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: SwarmResearch: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Open-Ended Discovery
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: SWARMRESEARCH introduces an orchestrator-subagent architecture for LLM-driven open-ended discovery that uses Git branching to maintain parallel code lineages and prevent premature convergence. The framework demonstrates strong empirical results, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines like EvoX and CORAL on 13 of 15 mathematical, heuristic, and systems optimization tasks. The key insight is that isolating agent context via separate Git branches—rather than relying on shared memory or long conversation histories—forces the exploration of diverse high-level approaches instead of greedy local micro-optimizations. This is highly relevant for our work in multi-agent evolutionary search and algorithm discovery, as adopting a Git-backed state management system could significantly improve the diversity and quality of our generated heuristics.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Symbolic Discovery of Iterative Algorithms: A Continuous Latent Space Bayesian Optimization Framework
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Liu and Mitrai propose a framework that maps discrete expression trees of iterative optimization algorithms into a continuous latent space using a Variational Autoencoder, enabling Bayesian Optimization to search for novel update rules. The results are backed by numbers but limited to a very small scale, showing that the method can discover a state-dependent step-size rule outperforming standard gradient descent on two 2-variable toy functions. The key insight is that transforming the discrete algorithm search space into a continuous one allows sample-efficient Bayesian Optimization to replace expensive combinatorial MINLP solvers. This is highly relevant to our research in continuous optimization for automated algorithm design, as it provides a concrete, non-LLM baseline methodology that we should compare against our generative approaches.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: The University of Texas at Austin

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: RAISE: LLM-based Automated Heuristic Design with Robust Adversary Instance Search
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: This paper introduces a bi-level evolutionary framework (RAISE) that couples an LLM-driven heuristic search with an LLM-free adversarial instance generator to evolve distributionally robust heuristics. The results are strongly backed by empirical data; on Online Bin Packing, RAISE reduces waste by up to 19x compared to standard LLM-based methods under severe distribution shifts, and shows similar robustness gains on vehicle routing and scheduling tasks. The key insight is to avoid expensive LLM calls for adversarial generation by using a lightweight, LLM-free evolutionary inner loop that parameterizes instance distributions as a mixture of basis functions and projects them onto an epsilon-ball around the training data. This is highly relevant for LLM evolutionary search, providing a concrete, compute-efficient mechanism to ensure evolved heuristics generalize to real-world distributional shifts rather than just memorizing the training set.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: University of Zurich, ETH Zurich

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: AlgoSkill: Learning to Design Algorithms by Scheduling Human-Like Skills
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: AlgoSkill frames LLM-based algorithm design as a sequential decision-making process, using Monte Carlo Tree Search to schedule a library of 20 typed algorithmic skills (e.g., constraint reading, state design, complexity refinement) guided by verification feedback. The method is backed by strong empirical results, significantly improving time-optimality and correctness over direct generation and free-form refinement on competitive programming and combinatorial optimization benchmarks (e.g., +44% time-optimality on a rule-based benchmark). The key insight is that constraining the LLM's search space to a discrete set of verifiable, typed algorithmic skills—rather than free-form code mutations—makes the search process more interpretable and efficient. This is highly relevant for LLM evolutionary search and automated algorithm discovery; the community could adopt typed skill operators as mutation strategies to improve sample efficiency and structural correctness in search-based frameworks.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Emory University, The University of Tokyo, LocationMind

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: MeEvo: Metacognitive Evolution Combined with Natural Evolution for Automatic Heuristic Design
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: MeEvo is an automatic heuristic design framework that cyclically alternates between Natural Evolution (LLM-mediated crossover and mutation on code) and Metacognitive Evolution (LLM reflection on accumulated reasoning and fitness history). Backed by extensive experiments, it significantly outperforms state-of-the-art LLM-based methods like FunSearch, EoH, and ReEvo across five optimization problems, including routing and complex constrained tasks, though at a roughly 7x higher token cost. The key insight is the explicit separation of reasoning traces (treated as heritable genotype) from executable code (phenotype), utilizing a two-step pipeline where the LLM first generates a strategic 'Meta Insight' from historical data before mapping it to new code. This is highly relevant to our work in LLM evolutionary search, providing a concrete architectural blueprint for integrating persistent memory and metacognitive reflection to improve search efficiency and escape local optima.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: University of Nottingham, University of Nottingham Ningbo China

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: CHIA: An open-source framework for principled, agentic AI-driven hardware/software co-design research
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Cui et al. introduce CHIA, an open-source, Ray-based framework for orchestrating and scaling agentic AI and evolutionary search workflows across heterogeneous compute clusters. The authors demonstrate strong empirical results in hardware design, such as automatically implementing RISC-V extensions that pass 25+ trillion instructions of SPEC06 and achieving a 2x frequency increase in critical path optimization. The key insight is the framework's architectural design, which uses graph-based orchestration with built-in caching, bypassing, and fault tolerance to solve major ergonomic and scalability bottlenecks in long-running LLM evolutionary search. This is highly relevant for our work in scaling multi-agent optimization and LLM evolutionary search, as the engineering patterns used to manage distributed evaluator nodes can directly inform our infrastructure.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: University of California, Berkeley

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Scientific discovery as meta-optimization: a combinatorial optimization case study
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Zhang et al. introduce a multi-agent meta-optimization framework that co-evolves both algorithm designs and their evaluation criteria using Monte Carlo Graph Search. The results are backed by strong empirical evidence, showing a reduction in the scaling exponent of a 3-SAT MemComputing solver from N^2.51 to N^1.33, yielding a 67x speedup at N=1810. The key insight is 'consensus objective aggregation', which combines multiple LLM-generated proxy objectives via correlation-weighted voting and age decay to create a stable, self-correcting fitness signal that resists reward hacking. This is a fundamental advance for LLM evolutionary search, providing a concrete method to dynamically improve evaluation strategies and prevent the search from exploiting flawed proxy metrics.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: University of California San Diego

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: AlgoEvolve: LLM-driven Meta-evolution of Algorithmic Trading Programs
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: This paper introduces a bi-level LLM evolutionary framework that synthesizes algorithmic trading programs in an inner loop while a meta-evolutionary outer loop optimizes the search prompts guiding the synthesis. The results are backed by empirical backtesting, showing the meta-evolutionary approach achieves a 5.60 annualized Sharpe ratio and successfully escapes the 'zero-trade' stagnation trap that plagues static-prompt baselines. The key insight is the use of a structured 'Prompt Genome' (separating mutation style, creative focus, constraints, and reasoning) combined with 'Informed Meta-Mutation,' where a Meta-LLM rewrites specific prompt genes based on a structured performance report (learning curves, error rates) from the inner loop. This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search; the team can directly adapt this meta-evolutionary outer loop to improve search efficiency and prevent stagnation when discovering heuristics for combinatorial optimization.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology, Delhi

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: EVOM: Agentic Meta-Evolution of Actor-Critic Architectures for Reinforcement Learning
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: EVOM introduces a bi-level LLM evolutionary search framework that designs actor-critic neural network architectures by using an LLM for mutation and crossover, while evaluating candidates via a low-fidelity reinforcement learning training loop. The authors demonstrate real empirical gains, outperforming manually designed architectures and baseline LLM-guided searches on MuJoCo continuous control tasks. The key insight is the explicit decoupling of the evolutionary search from full evaluation by using a low-budget proxy fitness signal, which makes population-level LLM search computationally feasible. This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search; adopting low-fidelity proxy evaluators (such as testing generated heuristics on small-scale routing or scheduling instances) could significantly improve our sample efficiency and search scalability.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Xidian University

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Project Auto-World: Towards Automated Benchmarking of Neural Relational Reasoners
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: This paper adapts FunSearch and an autonomous agentic loop to evolve Python priority functions that generate adversarial knowledge graph instances to stress-test neural relational reasoners. The authors provide strong empirical evidence showing both methods successfully drive down the accuracy of state-of-the-art Edge Transformers, and that training on these generated instances improves model robustness. The key insight is that a single autonomous coding agent iteratively refining a priority function can independently discover the same structural difficulty signals as a full population-based FunSearch pipeline, and can even break models that FunSearch fails to challenge. This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search and automated benchmarking, as it suggests agentic iterative refinement can be a viable, sometimes superior, alternative to complex population-based evolution.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Cardiff University, University of Pennsylvania

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Discovering Crystal Structure Prediction Algorithms with an AI Co-Scientist
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: This paper introduces HACO, an AI co-scientist system that uses tree-based LLM search and sparse human steering to discover a novel masked generative model (MaskGXT) for crystal structure prediction. The results are backed by strong empirical evidence, achieving state-of-the-art match rates (79.06% METRe) on standard MP-20 and MPTS-52 benchmarks compared to continuous diffusion baselines. The key insight is the system's architecture for 'sparse human steering'—where humans inject high-level objectives or mechanisms while the agent handles code implementation—combined with a 'cross-domain idea operator' that explicitly searches literature outside the target domain to seed the evolutionary tree. This is highly relevant to our research in LLM evolutionary search; the team should evaluate adopting this specific orchestrator pattern to improve observability and human-in-the-loop intervention in our automated algorithm design systems.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: KAIST

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Towards Diverse Scientific Hypothesis Search with Large Language Models
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: This paper introduces EvoDiverse, a parallel-tempered evolutionary framework that maintains multiple candidate pools at different selection pressures (temperatures) and exchanges them to balance exploration and exploitation in LLM-based search. The results are rigorously backed by empirical data across molecular, equation, and algorithm discovery (e.g., circle packing), demonstrating significant improvements in both solution quality and diversity under fixed evaluation budgets compared to standard single-pool or isolated-ensemble baselines. The key insight is the use of a Metropolis-Hastings acceptance gate for swapping candidates between high-temperature (exploratory) and low-temperature (exploitative) pools, which prevents disruptive candidates from destroying the exploitative pool while still allowing productive information flow. This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search and automated algorithm design, offering a principled, easy-to-implement architectural pattern to prevent premature convergence and improve sample efficiency.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: University of Cambridge, University of California, Berkeley, Microsoft Research New England, Carnegie Mellon University, Georgia Institute of Technology, Virginia Tech

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Beyond Static Evaluation: Co-Evolutionary Mechanisms for LLM-Driven Strategy Evolution in Adversarial Games
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Li et al. introduce an LLM-driven code evolution framework for multi-agent adversarial games that combats search stagnation using evaluator co-evolution, hierarchical deep evaluation, and weakness pressure. The results are rigorously backed by empirical data, demonstrating a 20% performance gain over existing baselines in a 3v3 capture-the-flag environment and securing 1st place in an AAMAS competition. The key insight is that static evaluation in LLM code evolution leads to overfitting; dynamically updating the test pool with past champions and up-weighting the hardest test cases (weakness pressure) sustains selective pressure and yields more robust algorithmic innovations. This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search, offering concrete, implementable techniques to improve fitness signals and evaluation efficiency when evolving complex heuristics.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Baidu AI Cloud, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Peking University, The University of Sydney, Southeast University

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: MLEvolve: A Self-Evolving Framework for Automated Machine Learning Algorithm Discovery
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: MLEvolve is a multi-agent framework for automated algorithm discovery that replaces standard tree search with Progressive Monte Carlo Graph Search (MCGS) and integrates retrospective memory with hierarchical code generation. Backed by strong empirical numbers, it achieves a state-of-the-art 65.3% medal rate on MLE-Bench in half the standard time and outperforms AlphaEvolve on 11 of 15 mathematical optimization tasks. The key insight is the Progressive MCGS architecture, which enables cross-branch information flow (fusion and aggregation) and uses an entropy-based schedule to shift from broad exploration to elite-guided exploitation, effectively solving the branch isolation problem. This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search and multi-agent optimization, providing concrete, implementable mechanisms for memory reuse and cross-trajectory crossover that improve sample efficiency and search quality.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, East China Normal University

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Adaptive Auto-Harness: Sustained Self-Improvement for Agentic System Deployment on Open-Ended Task Streams
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Adaptive Auto-Harness introduces a framework for open-ended task streams that uses a stateful multi-agent evolver, a git-based harness tree for solve-time routing, and human-in-the-loop steering to prevent overfitting to early tasks. The results are rigorously backed by empirical data across three diverse benchmarks, showing significant improvements over baselines like A-Evolve and Meta-Harness. The key insight is the transition from a single dense harness to a git-based harness tree, where the evolver creates regime-specific branches for prompts and tools, and a solve-time router selects the optimal branch per task. This directly addresses the artifact dilution problem and is highly relevant to our focus on continuous learning, persistent memory, and expert-in-the-loop observability in LLM evolutionary search.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Amazon, Emory University, UIUC, The Pennsylvania State University, Northeastern University

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: HarnessForge: Joint Harness and Policy Evolution for Adaptive Agent Systems
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: HarnessForge co-evolves an LLM agent's external execution harness (code for planning, action, memory) and its internal reasoning policy (via LoRA adapters) using a meta-agent for fault-guided tailoring. The results are backed by strong empirical evidence, showing up to 12% improvement on API and QA benchmarks using Qwen3-4B/8B, outperforming both search-only (e.g., AFlow, ADAS) and policy-only (e.g., GRPO, RLOO) baselines. The key insight is the sample-efficient co-evolution loop: using the meta-agent to evolve the code structure, filtering for successful trajectories, and immediately reusing those trajectories to fine-tune a harness-specific LoRA adapter without requiring additional rollouts. This is highly relevant for LLM evolutionary search, providing a concrete architecture for combining code-level evolutionary search with weight-level policy adaptation.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Tsinghua University, Beihang University

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: LLM-Driven Co-Evolutionary Automated Heuristic Design for Bi-Component Coupled Combinatorial Optimization
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: CoEvo-AHD introduces a dual-population co-evolutionary framework that uses LLMs to automatically design and co-evolve paired heuristics for bi-component combinatorial optimization problems like the Traveling Thief Problem. The results are backed by empirical numbers, showing competitive performance against traditional metaheuristics on small-to-medium instances, though it trails specialized state-of-the-art solvers on large-scale instances. The key insight is the use of 'cross-component joint crossover' and a 'shared information memory' dictionary, which allow the LLM to rewrite highly synergistic operator pairs together and pass soft search guidance between heterogeneous components. This is highly relevant for our work in multi-agent LLM evolutionary search, providing concrete architectural patterns for co-evolving interdependent algorithmic components.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Xi’an Jiao Tong University, Northwestern Polytechnical University

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: MetaEvo: A Meta-Optimization Framework for Experience-Driven Agent Evolution
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: MetaEvo introduces a two-stage framework for agent evolution that first fine-tunes an LLM via Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to improve its ability to abstract revision principles, and then iteratively accumulates these principles in a structured memory. The approach is backed by strong empirical results, demonstrating a 9.6% absolute accuracy gain on GSM8K for LLaMA-3.1-8B and consistent improvements across MATH, MMLU, and BBH compared to baselines like SE-GPT. The key insight is the 'meta-optimization' step: using a stronger model to generate preferred principles and applying DPO to the base model so it learns how to extract actionable, contrast-driven feedback rather than just memorizing task-specific corrections. This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search; the team could directly adapt the DPO-based meta-optimization and Contrast-Driven Abstraction to train 'evolver' agents, thereby improving the quality of heuristic revisions and overall sample efficiency.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Beijing Institute of Technology, BIT Southeast Academy of Information Technology

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: AI-PROPELLER: Warehouse-Scale Interprocedural Code Layout Optimization with AlphaEvolve
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: AI-PROPELLER applies an AlphaEvolve-based framework to discover fine-grained, interprocedural code layout heuristics for warehouse-scale binaries. The results are backed by rigorous hardware metrics, demonstrating statistically significant execution time reductions of 0.23% to 1.6% on massive applications like LLVM Clang and production search services. The key insight is the extreme lengths taken to ensure a noise-free reward signal for the LLM evolutionary loop; by locking CPU frequencies and disabling ASLR/Turbo Boost, they reduced run-to-run variance to under 0.05%, allowing the agent to accurately learn from micro-optimizations. This is highly relevant to our work in LLM evolutionary search, as it provides a concrete blueprint for scaling these methods to combinatorially massive search spaces by engineering high-fidelity empirical reward signals.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Google DeepMind, Google, University of California, Riverside

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Evolve as a Team: Collaborative Self-Evolution for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: This paper introduces Meta-Team, a framework for multi-agent system self-evolution where agents retain local execution contexts and communicate post-task to collaboratively update individual behaviors, interaction profiles, and team coordination rules. The approach is backed by strong empirical results, showing an average 6.3% improvement over the strongest MAS evolution baseline across six challenging, long-horizon benchmarks (including SWE-bench Pro and GAIA). The key insight is that flattening multi-agent trajectories for a centralized meta-optimizer creates a context bottleneck and degrades failure attribution; instead, evolution should be distributed, allowing agents to reflect locally and exchange evidence to pinpoint failures. This is highly relevant for our work in multi-agent evolutionary search, as the decentralized reflection and multi-scale update mechanism provides a concrete architectural blueprint for improving sample efficiency and credit assignment in complex optimization tasks.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Tencent, Zhejiang University, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Vector Policy Optimization: Training for Diversity Improves Test-Time Search
LLMs for Algorithm Design.front_name: Adaptive and Meta-Evolutionary LLM Frameworks for Algorithmic Discovery
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Bahlous-Boldi et al. introduce Vector Policy Optimization (VPO), an RL post-training method that trains LLMs to generate diverse candidate sets by combining multi-answer autoregressive generation with stochastic reward scalarization. The results are rigorously backed by empirical data, demonstrating that VPO continuously scales with test-time compute and successfully solves hard LiveCodeBench problems inside an AlphaEvolve-style evolutionary loop where standard GRPO completely stalls. The key insight is that collapsing vector rewards (such as per-test-case correctness) into a single scalar during RL causes mode collapse; instead, sampling random weightings from a Dirichlet distribution forces the policy to maintain a Pareto-diverse set of strategies. This is a fundamental advance for LLM evolutionary search, as applying VPO to mutator or generator models directly addresses sample efficiency and prevents premature convergence in automated algorithm design.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: MIT, Sakana AI, Improbable AI Lab, MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: optimize_anything: A Universal API for Optimizing any Text Parameter
LLMs for Algorithm Design.front_name: Architectural and Feedback Innovations in LLM-Guided Evolutionary Algorithm Discovery
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Agrawal et al. introduce optimize_anything, a unified LLM-based evolutionary search API that optimizes arbitrary text artifacts (code, prompts, agent architectures) using Pareto-based selection and diagnostic side information. Results are highly rigorous and backed by numbers, including a controlled ablation showing it beats OpenEvolve on circle packing in 3x fewer evaluations, and achieving SOTA on ARC-AGI (89.5%), cloud scheduling, and CUDA kernel generation. The most actionable takeaway is the combination of multi-task search with a shared Pareto frontier, allowing optimization patterns discovered in one task to transfer to related tasks, alongside the formalization of Side Information (SI) as a first-class 'text gradient' to drive targeted mutations rather than blind evolution. This is a landmark paper for LLM evolutionary search; the team should immediately evaluate adopting the multi-task Pareto frontier and structured SI contracts to improve sample efficiency and cross-problem transfer in our own automated algorithm design frameworks.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: UC Berkeley, MIT

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Property-Guided LLM Program Synthesis for Planning
LLMs for Algorithm Design.front_name: Architectural and Feedback Innovations in LLM-Guided Evolutionary Algorithm Discovery
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: This paper replaces scalar fitness scores in LLM heuristic synthesis with a counterexample-guided repair loop that checks formal properties and feeds specific failure states back to the LLM. The results are backed by strong empirical evidence on 10 planning domains, showing a 7.4x reduction in LLM generation cost, a 1000x reduction in evaluation compute, and higher task coverage compared to the previous sample-and-select state of the art. The key insight is that using verifiable properties to generate concrete, localized counterexamples (e.g., 'at state X, your heuristic gave value Y, but successors gave Z') is vastly more sample-efficient than end-to-end scalar rewards. This is highly relevant for LLM evolutionary search and automated algorithm design; the community should investigate defining checkable properties for routing or scheduling heuristics to replace or augment standard scalar fitness evaluations, drastically reducing LLM sample complexity.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: University of Oxford, Linköping University, Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: MetaAgent-X : Breaking the Ceiling of Automatic Multi-Agent Systems via End-to-End Reinforcement Learning
LLMs for Algorithm Design.front_name: Adaptive and Meta-Evolutionary LLM Frameworks for Algorithmic Discovery
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: MetaAgent-X is an end-to-end reinforcement learning framework that jointly optimizes a meta-agent (Designer) that generates multi-agent workflows and the downstream agents (Executors) that run them. The results are backed by strong empirical evidence, showing up to 21.7% improvement over baselines on math and code benchmarks using Qwen3-8B. The key insight is the Executor-Designer Hierarchical Rollout combined with stagewise co-evolution: by sampling M designs and executing each N times, the system isolates the designer's reward from the executor's reward, while alternating training phases stabilizes the non-stationary RL environment. This is highly relevant to our work in LLM evolutionary search and multi-agent optimization, providing a concrete, implementable architecture for RL-infused meta-agent training and credit assignment.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Amazon AGI, UCSD, Oregon State University, Pennsylvania State University, AG2AI, Inc.

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Adapting AlphaEvolve to Optimize Fully Homomorphic Encryption on TPUs
LLMs for Algorithm Design.front_name: Architectural and Feedback Innovations in LLM-Guided Evolutionary Algorithm Discovery
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: This paper applies the AlphaEvolve framework to automatically optimize Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) kernels for TPU execution, using LLM-driven code generation guided by hardware-in-the-loop latency feedback and strict correctness checks. The results are real and backed by physical hardware deployments, achieving up to a 2.5x speedup over human-engineered state-of-the-art baselines on TPUv5e chips. The key insight is that optimizing isolated operations often fails to yield end-to-end speedups; instead, co-evolving multiple components and scoring them against complete system execution, while feeding back low-level execution traces (e.g., Xprof) to the LLM, is necessary to discover non-obvious compiler and scheduling optimizations. This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search, as the methodology of using execution traces as diagnostic feedback and enforcing end-to-end co-evolution directly informs how we should structure reward signals and evaluation environments for automated algorithm design.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Google DeepMind, Google, Georgia Institute of Technology

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Effective Harness Engineering for Algorithm Discovery with Coding Agents
LLMs for Algorithm Design.front_name: Architectural and Feedback Innovations in LLM-Guided Evolutionary Algorithm Discovery
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Vesper introduces a novel execution harness for LLM-driven algorithm discovery that replaces stateless LLM API calls with autonomous coding agents capable of multi-step reasoning, debugging, and codebase inspection. Backed by concrete numbers, Vesper outperforms OpenEvolve and matches AlphaEvolve on the Circle Packing benchmark under strict token and cost budgets, achieving higher scores with significantly fewer generated algorithms. The key insight is that under a fixed budget, scaling the reasoning quality per algorithm (using expensive, multi-step coding agents) is vastly more efficient than scaling the number of evolutionary generations (using cheap, single-shot API calls). This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search; the team should immediately evaluate shifting our mutation operators from single-shot prompts to agentic loops and adopt Git worktree isolation for safe, parallel execution.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: NEC Corporation

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: EvolveMem:Self-Evolving Memory Architecture via AutoResearch for LLM Agents
LLMs for Algorithm Design.front_name: Architectural and Feedback Innovations in LLM-Guided Evolutionary Algorithm Discovery
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: EVOLVEMEM introduces a self-evolving memory architecture for LLM agents that autonomously optimizes its retrieval infrastructure (e.g., fusion weights, context budgets) using an LLM-powered diagnosis module that analyzes failure logs. The results are backed by strong empirical evidence, showing a 25.7% relative improvement over the state-of-the-art on the LoCoMo benchmark and positive transfer to MemBench. The key insight is treating the retrieval configuration as a structured action space and using an LLM to propose targeted adjustments based on per-question failure logs, safeguarded by a revert-on-regression mechanism. This is highly relevant to our work in LLM evolutionary search and multi-agent memory systems, as the closed-loop AutoResearch methodology can be directly adapted to evolve hyperparameters or retrieval strategies in our own agentic architectures.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: UNC-Chapel Hill, UC Berkeley, UCSC

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Harnessing Agentic Evolution
LLMs for Algorithm Design.front_name: Architectural and Feedback Innovations in LLM-Guided Evolutionary Algorithm Discovery
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Zhang et al. introduce AEVO, a framework that formulates LLM evolutionary search as an interactive environment where a meta-agent edits the underlying search procedure or agent context rather than directly generating candidate solutions. The results are backed by strong empirical evidence, achieving state-of-the-art performance on Anthropic's Kernel optimization task (1138 cycles) and outperforming baselines like OpenEvolve and HyperAgents across multiple open-ended discovery and reasoning benchmarks. The key insight is separating the candidate generation loop from a meta-editing phase, allowing the system to dynamically revise its own selection rules, feedback summaries, and memory structures when search plateaus. This is a must-read for our work in LLM evolutionary search, as it provides a concrete, actionable architecture for 'evolving the evolver' and maintaining long-horizon search without agent drift.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Tsinghua University, Université de Montréal & Mila, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou), Nanyang Technological University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Singapore University of Technology and Design, DeepWisdom

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: Graph-Grounded Optimization: Rao-Family Metaheuristics, Classical OR, and SLM-Driven Formulation over Knowledge Graphs
LLMs for Algorithm Design.front_name: Architectural and Feedback Innovations in LLM-Guided Evolutionary Algorithm Discovery
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: This paper introduces a graph-grounded optimization paradigm where operations research problem components are sourced directly from property knowledge graphs via Cypher queries, rather than from lossy natural language descriptions. The results are backed by strong empirical numbers across 7 real-world KGs, demonstrating that while classical solvers and metaheuristics succeed, frontier SLMs (including the MILP-tuned OptiMind) fail almost completely at zero-shot formulation. The key insight is the identification of a 'data-binding pathology': LLMs generate syntactically valid optimization code that silently fails or returns trivial solutions because it binds to hallucinated data structures instead of the actual operational database. This is highly relevant for our OR benchmarking and evaluation work, as it proves that evaluating LLMs purely on text-to-math translation ignores the critical, failure-prone step of grounding the formulation in real-world data schemas.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Samyama.ai

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: CVEvolve: Autonomous Algorithm Discovery for Unstructured Scientific Data Processing
LLMs for Algorithm Design.front_name: Adaptive and Meta-Evolutionary LLM Frameworks for Algorithmic Discovery
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: CVEvolve is an LLM-based evolutionary search framework that autonomously discovers data-processing algorithms using a generate-tune-evolve loop, lineage-aware sampling, and SQL-backed persistent memory. The results are backed by strong empirical evidence, showing significant improvements over baselines, such as reducing X-ray image registration error from 0.98 to 0.12. The key insight is the use of a relational SQL database to manage search history and lineage (avoiding context bloat) combined with a dedicated holdout-test agent to prevent over-optimization on small development sets. This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search; the team could directly adopt the SQL memory architecture and holdout-test agent to improve the scalability and generalization of our own automated heuristic design frameworks.
LLMs for Algorithm Design.affiliations: Argonne National Laboratory

LLMs for Algorithm Design.title: RubricEM: Meta-RL with Rubric-guided Policy Decomposition beyond Verifiable Rewards
LLMs for Algorithm Design.front_name: Architectural and Feedback Innovations in LLM-Guided Evolutionary Algorithm Discovery
LLMs for Algorithm Design.brief: Li et al. introduce RubricEM, an RL framework for long-horizon LLM agents that uses dynamically generated rubrics to structure trajectories, assign stage-wise process rewards via Stage-Structured GRPO, and train a reflection memory bank for cross-episode transfer. The results are rigorously backed by numbers, showing their 8B model outperforming 30B+ open models and approaching proprietary systems on four long-form research benchmarks. The key insight is that rubrics can serve as a shared interface across the entire RL loop, acting simultaneously as structural priors for planning, dynamic process reward models for intermediate credit assignment, and structured memory for experience reuse. This is highly relevant for our work in LLM evolutionary search and multi-agent optimization, as the asynchronous reflection pipeline and stage-structured credit assignment directly address our core challenges in sample efficiency, process reward modeling, and persistent memory across search runs.
