Generative AI for OR.title: LP Mining with LP2Graph: A Use Case for Railway Rescheduling
Generative AI for OR.brief: Maurischat et al. introduce LP2Graph, a deterministic pipeline to extract, homologize, and cluster published LP/MILP formulations into a canonical graph representation to build a structural taxonomy. While the current preprint only demonstrates the end-to-end pipeline on a small 10-formulation fixture set (with an 8,957-formulation corpus pending), the round-trip translation and cross-solver validation methodology is rigorously defined. The key insight is that representing MILPs as typed variable-equation graphs allows for deterministic structural comparison (schema graph isomorphism) independent of author notation. This is highly relevant for OR benchmarking and evaluation, as it provides a concrete mechanism to structurally compare LLM-generated OR models against ground-truth formulations rather than relying solely on execution accuracy.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: TU Dresden

Generative AI for OR.title: OptiAgent: End-to-End Optimization Modeling via Multi-Agent Iterative Refinement
Generative AI for OR.brief: OptiAgent proposes a multi-agent framework that translates natural language Operations Research problem descriptions into mathematical formulations and executable code using specialized agents and four targeted feedback loops. The results are backed by strong empirical evidence, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy on 3 out of 4 standard OR modeling benchmarks (including 70.65% on the challenging LogiOR dataset using GPT-5.4). The key insight is the explicit separation of mathematical validation (checking index quantification, dimensional consistency, and variable connectivity) from code generation, which allows the system to catch and self-correct structural errors before runtime execution. This is highly relevant for our research in OR benchmarking and multi-agent optimization modeling, as the specific validation strategies and feedback loop architecture can be directly integrated into our evaluation pipelines to improve formulation accuracy.

Generative AI for OR.title: A$^{2}$utoLPBench: An Auto-Generated, Agent-Friendly LP Benchmark via Inverse-KKT Construction
Generative AI for OR.brief: This paper introduces a dynamic, auto-generated benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on linear programming by using inverse-KKT conditions to construct problems with known optima without requiring solver calls. The results are rigorously backed by numbers, demonstrating a smooth difficulty curve up to 40x40 matrices and revealing an 87 percentage-point performance cliff for state-of-the-art models that static benchmarks fail to expose. The key insight is that using inverse optimization—sampling the optimal solution and duals first, then deriving the constraints and objective—allows for infinite, zero-cost, mathematically certified benchmark generation that completely bypasses training data contamination. This is highly relevant to our work in OR benchmarking and evaluation, as the inverse-construction methodology could fundamentally upgrade how we generate symbolic OR modeling tasks.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

Generative AI for OR.title: Uncertainty-Aware Simulation-Based Inference for Operations Research with Large Language Models
Generative AI for OR.brief: Liang et al. introduce a training-free inference framework that improves LLM-based operations research modeling by using short lookahead simulations and importance resampling to select intermediate generation steps based on downstream uncertainty. The results are backed by solid empirical evidence, showing up to a 17.6% absolute correctness improvement on complex OR benchmarks over standard sampling with an 8B model. The key insight is that the quality of a partial formulation or code block can be accurately estimated by measuring the entropy or probability concentration of short future rollouts from the frozen base model, bypassing the need for full-trajectory evaluations or trained verifiers. This is highly relevant to our work in OR modeling and LLM evolutionary search, as it provides a scalable method to generate reliable step-level fitness signals without requiring expensive process reward model training.

Generative AI for OR.title: EvoOptiGraph: Weakness-Driven Coevolution via Graph-Based Structural Generation for Optimization Modeling
Generative AI for OR.brief: Kang et al. introduce EvoOptiGraph, a framework that coevolves an LLM and its training data for natural-language-to-optimization modeling. The authors demonstrate that an 8B model fine-tuned with this method outperforms GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 across six OR benchmarks, backed by rigorous ablation studies. The key insight is the weakness-driven generation loop: they train an XGBoost classifier on the structural graph features of instances the LLM fails to solve, then use the resulting SHAP values to bias the evolutionary algorithm's fitness function toward generating similar hard instances. This dynamic, targeted data generation approach is highly relevant to our work in LLM evolutionary search and OR benchmarking, offering a concrete mechanism to improve sample efficiency and address model blind spots during RL.

Generative AI for OR.title: COOPA: A Modular LLM Agent Architecture for Operations Research Problems
Generative AI for OR.brief: COOPA is a multi-agent LLM architecture for operations research modeling that uses iterative generation, dimension-specific confidence scoring with max-min selection, and multi-solver dispatch to translate natural language into executable optimization code. Backed by solid empirical results, it achieves a 64.8% macro-average accuracy across three OR benchmarks and eight LLMs, outperforming existing baselines like OR-LLM-Agent and OptiTree. The key insight is the max-min confidence selection criterion, which evaluates intermediate formulations across four specific dimensions (parameters, variables, objective, constraints) to catch structural errors before code generation. This is highly relevant for our work in OR benchmarking and multi-agent optimization modeling, as it provides both a strong baseline architecture and a practical heuristic approach to process-level reward modeling for LLM reasoning.

Generative AI for OR.title: MiniOpt: Reasoning to Model and Solve General Optimization Problems with Limited Resources
Generative AI for OR.brief: MiniOpt trains small-scale LLMs (3B/7B) to formulate and solve optimization problems using a two-stage Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Reward (RLVR) framework. The results are rigorously backed by numbers across 8 OR benchmarks, showing that MiniOpt-7B achieves a 64.76% average solving accuracy, outperforming general 14B models and competing with DeepSeek-R1 while using significantly fewer tokens. The key insight is the hierarchical OptReward function, which sequentially scores formatting, a 5-element mathematical tuple, and final execution accuracy, enabling stable RL training without expensive human CoT annotations. Furthermore, modifying GRPO with asymmetric clipping and removing the KL penalty significantly improves exploration in complex reasoning tasks. This is highly relevant for our work in OR benchmarking and RL-infused LLM optimization, as the verifiable reward pipeline and GRPO modifications offer concrete techniques for improving sample efficiency and training stability.

Generative AI for OR.title: ORAgentBench: Can LLM Agents Solve Challenging Operations Research Tasks End to End?
Generative AI for OR.brief: This paper introduces ORAgentBench, an execution-grounded benchmark of 107 tasks that evaluates autonomous LLM agents on their ability to solve end-to-end operations research problems from raw data to validated decision artifacts. Extensive empirical results across 14 frontier models show that the best agent achieves only a 35.5% pass rate, with failures dominated by strategic modeling errors rather than coding bugs. The key insight is the benchmark's rigorous separation of hard-constraint feasibility and normalized objective quality, which exposes a critical gap where agents can generate executable code but fail to make the structural choices needed for high-quality optimization. This is essential reading for the team's OR benchmarking and evaluation research, as it establishes a new standard by moving beyond static text-to-formulation tasks to dynamic, multi-file execution environments.

Generative AI for OR.title: StarOR: Synergizing Tree Search and Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for Optimization Modeling
Generative AI for OR.brief: StarOR integrates Monte Carlo Tree Search with test-time reinforcement learning to dynamically update a transient LoRA adapter during optimization modeling. The results are rigorously backed by empirical data across five benchmarks, demonstrating that a 4B parameter model can outperform GPT-4 and DeepSeek-R1. The key insight is using MCTS sibling nodes as a local comparison batch for GRPO to update the policy weights during inference, guided by an unsupervised multi-faceted reward (execution, semantic consensus, structural consistency, and test-case robustness). This is highly relevant for LLM evolutionary search and OR modeling, as it provides a concrete, sample-efficient mechanism for RL-infused search that prevents the model from repeatedly exploring flawed trajectories.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Southeast University, Northwest A&F University

Generative AI for OR.title: WARA: Toward Automated Wireless Optimization Research with Closed-Loop LLM Agents
Generative AI for OR.brief: WARA is an end-to-end multi-agent framework that automates wireless optimization research by generating mathematical models, designing algorithms, executing experiments, and writing manuscripts. The results are backed by quantitative evaluations, showing a 31-point improvement in manuscript validity over one-shot LLM generation, though it still trails human-authored papers. The key insight is the use of 'artifact-mediated control' with 'frozen contracts', where upstream decisions (like mathematical formulations) are validated and locked before downstream agents (like algorithm designers) can proceed, enabling localized repair instead of full-pipeline restarts. This architectural pattern is highly relevant for multi-agent optimization and automated algorithm design, as adopting strict contract-freezing could significantly improve the stability and sample efficiency of LLM-based operations research pipelines.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, City University of Hong Kong, Sun Yat-Sen University

Generative AI for OR.title: Beyond Objective Equivalence: Constraint Injection for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling on Vehicle Routing Problems
Generative AI for OR.brief: This paper introduces constraint injection—using feasible and one-constraint-violating probes—as a dual verifier alongside differential testing to train and evaluate LLMs for vehicle routing optimization modeling. The results are highly rigorous and backed by strong empirical evidence; their 8B model (VRPCoder-GRPO) achieves 93% Pass@1 across 21 VRP variants, outperforming Gemini-3.1-Pro and surpassing prior OR-LLMs by 78 points. The key insight is that objective equivalence is structurally blind to silent constraint omissions, whereas targeted, constraint-violating probes provide a much denser, more accurate reward signal for RL and data filtering. This is a must-read for our work in OR benchmarking and LLM evolutionary search, as it provides a concrete, implementable method to construct better fitness evaluators and process reward models for constraint-dense optimization tasks.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Baidu Inc., Beihang University

Generative AI for OR.title: OptSkills: Learning Generalizable Optimization Skills from Problem Archetypes via Cluster-Based Distillation
Generative AI for OR.brief: OPTSKILLS is an LLM agent system that improves optimization modeling by clustering problems according to their underlying mathematical archetypes and distilling reusable skills from solving trajectories. The method is backed by strong empirical results, achieving a state-of-the-art 68.27% micro-averaged accuracy across five OR benchmarks and outperforming DeepSeek-V3.2-Thinking on the large-scale MIPLIB-NL dataset. The key insight is that raw problem text embeddings fail to group structurally identical optimization problems; instead, extracting scenario-agnostic structural keywords before embedding enables highly effective cluster-based skill distillation and drastically reduces memory redundancy. This is highly relevant for our research in LLM-based OR modeling and persistent memory architectures, as the archetype-based clustering provides a concrete mechanism to organize and retrieve generalized optimization strategies without overfitting to specific narratives.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Ant Group, East China Normal University, Shanghai Innovation Institute

Generative AI for OR.title: Opt-Verifier: Unleashing the Power of LLMs for Optimization Modeling via Dual-Side Verification
Generative AI for OR.brief: Opt-Verifier is a multi-agent LLM framework that improves automated operations research modeling through dual-side verification: checking structural consistency via back-translation and logical validity by semantically critiquing the numerical solutions of toy instantiations. Backed by strong empirical results, it achieves a significant improvement in solving accuracy over standard prompting and outperforms SOTA models like OpenAI-o1 and OptiMUS across benchmarks like NL4Opt, ComplexOR, and IndustryOR. The most valuable takeaway is the solution-side verification mechanism. Instead of just checking if solver code compiles, the system instantiates the parameterized model with toy data, solves it, translates the numerical output back to natural language, and uses an LLM to catch logical absurdities (e.g., a closed warehouse shipping goods). This is directly applicable to our research in OR benchmarking and multi-agent optimization modeling, offering a concrete method for generating high-fidelity process reward signals without requiring ground-truth labels.

Generative AI for OR.title: OR-Space: A Full-Lifecycle Workspace Benchmark for Industrial Optimization Agents
Generative AI for OR.brief: Zhou et al. introduce OR-Space, a benchmark that evaluates LLM agents on industrial optimization tasks within persistent multi-artifact workspaces (documents, data, code) across three lifecycle stages: Build, Revise, and Explain. The results are backed by extensive empirical evaluation across 20 models, demonstrating that even frontier models struggle with workspace-grounded data mapping (e.g., Gemini 3.1 Pro achieves only 72% on Build) and that legacy code context can severely degrade performance for weaker models. The key insight is the shift from single-shot formulation to lifecycle evaluation; testing an agent's ability to revise existing models and explain solver outputs grounded in distributed artifacts exposes critical failure modes hidden by standard text-only benchmarks. This is highly relevant for our work in OR benchmarking and LLM reasoning evaluation, as it provides a more rigorous, realistic framework for measuring the practical readiness of optimization agents.

Generative AI for OR.title: OptiLoop: Coordination-in-the-Loop Verification and Repair for LLM-Generated Optimization Agents
Generative AI for OR.brief: OptiLoop verifies and repairs LLM-generated optimization agents by running short ADMM-style coordination episodes to extract behavioral evidence, such as price response and convergence, rather than relying solely on local execution checks. The results are backed by rigorous ablation on 80 supply chain scenarios, showing that the full pipeline improves objective match from 66% to 93% compared to local validation alone. The key insight is that local executability is insufficient for optimization code; semantic errors can be reliably detected by observing how the generated model responds to economic incentives like dual prices during multi-agent coordination. This is highly relevant for our work in multi-agent optimization and LLM reasoning evaluation. The team could adopt this coordination-in-the-loop behavioral testing as a sophisticated process reward signal when generating or evolving operations research models.

Generative AI for OR.title: VeriSimpl: Robust Optimization Modeling from Natural Language using Simplification-based Verification
Generative AI for OR.brief: VERISIMPL introduces a framework that verifies LLM-generated optimization models by using the solver to create simplified diagnostic queries (e.g., variable masking, constraint mutations) which the LLM then checks against the original natural language description. The results are backed by strong empirical evidence, showing consistent accuracy improvements (up to 17% over agentic baselines) across four OR benchmarks and providing a >90% precision self-verification signal. The key insight is to invert the standard verification workflow: instead of relying on the LLM to generate test cases, use the solver to generate concrete, simplified partial states, and use the LLM to verify these tractable states against the text prompt. This is highly relevant for our work in OR benchmarking and evaluation, and this solver-guided verification mechanism could be directly adapted as a high-quality Process Reward Model (PRM) to guide LLM evolutionary search when generating OR formulations.

Generative AI for OR.title: FrontierOR: Benchmarking LLMs'Capacity for Efficient Algorithm Design in Large-Scale Optimization
Generative AI for OR.brief: This paper introduces FrontierOR, a benchmark of 180 large-scale operations research tasks designed to evaluate whether LLMs can design efficient, scalable optimization algorithms rather than just monolithic mathematical formulations. Results are rigorously backed by empirical evaluations against Gurobi baselines, showing that one-shot frontier models achieve only 31% quality-time efficiency, whereas test-time compute via multi-agent evolutionary search frameworks improves this success rate to 50% on the hardest tasks. The key insight is that the bottleneck for frontier LLMs has shifted from writing executable code to algorithmic strategy; successful LLM agents must autonomously explore hybrid, decomposition, or matheuristic designs rather than relying on direct solver calls. This is a must-read as it provides a ready-to-use, rigorous evaluation suite for our LLM evolutionary search and multi-agent optimization frameworks, pushing the field's evaluation standard beyond simple formulation correctness.

Generative AI for OR.title: BBOWP-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Black-Box Optimization Word Problems
Generative AI for OR.brief: This paper introduces BBOWP-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating how well LLMs can infer search spaces and select optimization algorithms from natural-language descriptions of black-box optimization tasks. The results are backed by extensive empirical runs, demonstrating that while LLMs can select budget-appropriate algorithms, they struggle significantly to define valid search spaces when problem descriptions are ambiguous. The key insight is the Formulation Ranking Score (FRS) metric, which evaluates the quality of an LLM-generated search space and algorithm pair by comparing its downstream execution performance against a Monte Carlo-sampled reference distribution, providing a scale-invariant evaluation across diverse domains. This is highly relevant for our work in OR benchmarking and evaluation; the execution-based evaluation pipeline and FRS metric could be directly adapted to improve how we evaluate LLM reasoning on optimization modeling tasks.

Generative AI for OR.title: Models Can Model, But Can't Bind: Structured Grounding in Text-to-Optimization
Generative AI for OR.brief: This paper introduces Text2Opt-Bench, a scalable text-to-optimization benchmark, and demonstrates that LLM failures on large OR problems stem primarily from 'binding' (transcribing numerical data) rather than 'modeling' (formulating the math). The claims are backed by rigorous empirical results across 10+ models, showing that externalizing data to JSON (the BIND method) improves GPT-5-Nano accuracy from 59.1% to 82.4%, and that a 7B binding-specialist model outperforms end-to-end SFT and RL. The key insight is that the bottleneck in text-to-optimization is context retrieval and transcription, not mathematical reasoning; offloading numerical data to structured files for programmatic access bypasses this limitation entirely. This is highly relevant for our OR benchmarking and LLM reasoning evaluation efforts, as the modeling vs. binding paradigm should directly inform how we construct instances and evaluate LLMs in our own OR benchmarks.

Generative AI for OR.title: Learn2Zinc: Fine-tuning Small Language Models for Text-to-Model Translation in MiniZinc
Generative AI for OR.brief: This paper fine-tunes small language models (0.6B to 20B parameters) using a cross-model error bootstrapping dataset to translate natural language problem descriptions into executable MiniZinc constraint models. The results are backed by solid empirical evidence, showing that while out-of-the-box execution accuracy is near zero, the fine-tuned ensemble with self-reflection achieves 98% execution accuracy, though solution (semantic) accuracy plateaus at 35%. The key insight is the cross-model error bootstrapping technique, which effectively cures syntax failures in out-of-distribution domain-specific languages and isolates the remaining LLM reasoning bottlenecks into specific semantic failure modes like phantom variables and contradictory constraints. This is highly relevant for our research in OR benchmarking and symbolic OR modeling evaluation, as the error taxonomy and dataset curation strategy can directly inform how we design evaluations for LLM reasoning on optimization problems.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Brown University, Fidelity Investments

Generative AI for OR.title: PEARL: Solver-in-the-Loop Interactive Optimization Modeling from Natural Language
Generative AI for OR.brief: PEARL trains a compact LLM (4B parameters) using agentic reinforcement learning to iteratively draft, execute, and revise mathematical optimization models based on intermediate solver feedback. Backed by strong empirical numbers, the 4B PEARL model achieves a 69.71% macro-average Pass@1 across 8 OR benchmarks, outperforming the 685B DeepSeek-V3.2 model. The key insight is that instead of applying RL to score final outputs, RL (specifically GRPO with decoupled clipping) should be used to learn the control policy for the entire solve-debug-revise loop, allowing the model to learn when to execute code and how to interpret solver errors. This is highly relevant to our work in RL-infused LLM search and symbolic OR modeling, as it provides a concrete methodology for integrating deterministic solver feedback into the policy optimization pipeline to drastically improve sample efficiency and accuracy.

Generative AI for OR.title: TriVAL: A Tri-Validation Framework for Faithful Automatic Optimization Modeling
Generative AI for OR.brief: Fang et al. propose TriVAL, a multi-stage validation framework for translating natural language into executable optimization models, alongside a new 150-instance combinatorial optimization benchmark (NL4COP). The results are strongly backed by empirical evaluations, showing a 30%+ accuracy improvement over existing agentic baselines on complex combinatorial tasks. The key insight is formalizing the semantic specification as a tuple of facts, ambiguities, and resolutions, ensuring that implicit assumptions are explicitly resolved before mathematical formulation begins. This is highly relevant for our work in benchmarking and evaluating symbolic OR modeling, as the dataset and the ambiguity-resolution mechanism directly address the core challenges of evaluating LLM reasoning on complex OR problems.

Generative AI for OR.title: Formalize, Don't Optimize: The Heuristic Trap in LLM-Generated Combinatorial Solvers

Generative AI for OR.brief: Wang et al. evaluate frontier LLMs on a new 4,577-instance combinatorial optimization benchmark to compare solver-generation paradigms (Python, Python+OR-Tools, MiniZinc) and the impact of efficiency-oriented prompting. The results, backed by rigorous instance-level evaluation, demonstrate that LLMs achieve the highest correctness using the Python+OR-Tools API, whereas native Python suffers from high rates of silent failures. The key insight is the identification of the 'heuristic trap': prompting LLMs to optimize search zero-shot yields minimal speedups but sharply degrades correctness by injecting unverified bounds, local approximations, or overcomplicated constraints. This is highly relevant to our work in OR benchmarking and LLM evolutionary search. Specifically, the six documented failure modes provide a precise taxonomy of errors that our process reward models and evolutionary evaluators must be explicitly designed to detect and penalize.

Generative AI for OR.brief: This paper introduces AutoRO-Bench for evaluating LLM robust optimization reformulation and proposes AutoREM, a tuning-free memory-augmented LLM framework that uses offline adaptation to build a structured reformulation memory. The results are backed by strong empirical evidence, with AutoREM achieving 97.4% accuracy on in-distribution and 94.8% on out-of-distribution datasets, significantly outperforming baselines like ACE and ReasoningBank while using fewer tokens. The key insight is the offline memory adaptation pipeline—specifically the Dual-Check Commit (DCC) for mini-batch validation and Validation-Based Acceptance (VBA) for epoch-level rollbacks—which prevents the accumulation of harmful memory edits and ensures high-quality, reusable reasoning templates. This is highly relevant for our work in OR benchmarking and LLM evolutionary search, as the structured memory operators and validation gates offer a concrete blueprint for improving persistent memory and sample efficiency in self-improving LLM agents.

Generative AI for OR.title: Agentic MIP Research: Accelerated Constraint Handler Generation

Generative AI for OR.brief: Xu et al. propose an LLM agentic framework that autonomously generates, verifies, and tunes propagation-only constraint handlers for the SCIP MIP solver. Generative AI for OR.title: CHORUS: Zero-shot Hierarchical Retrieval and Orchestration for Generating Linear Programming Code

Generative AI for OR.brief: CHORUS introduces a RAG framework for generating Gurobi code that replaces standard code retrieval with a metadata-based approach, indexing code examples by generated keywords and summaries rather than raw syntax. On the NL4Opt-Code benchmark, this allows open-source models like Llama-3-70B to match GPT-4 performance (improving accuracy from ~23% to ~57%). The key takeaway for us is the effectiveness of 'metadata-augmented indexing'—bridging the semantic gap between natural language problem descriptions and rigid solver APIs by retrieving based on functional descriptions rather than code embeddings. We should apply this metadata indexing strategy to the code retrieval modules in our OR-Bench and AlgoEvo agents.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Queen's University

Generative AI for OR.title: OptimAI: Optimization from Natural Language Using LLM-Powered AI Agents
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Structured LLM-Driven Optimization Modeling via Verification and Self-Improving Agents
Generative AI for OR.brief: OptimAI introduces a multi-agent framework for translating natural language to optimization models, featuring a 'plan-before-code' stage and a novel **UCB-based debug scheduler**. Instead of linearly debugging a single solution, it treats debugging as a multi-armed bandit problem, dynamically allocating compute to different solution strategies based on a 'Decider' score and exploration term. While the combinatorial results (TSP a280) are trivial, the bandit mechanism is a highly effective heuristic for search control. We should steal this UCB scheduling logic for AlgoEvo to prevent agents from wasting tokens debugging fundamentally flawed heuristics.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: University of Maryland at College Park

Generative AI for OR.title: CO-Bench: Benchmarking Language Model Agents in Algorithm Search for Combinatorial Optimization
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Execution-Verified LLM Agents for OR Model and Algorithm Synthesis
Generative AI for OR.brief: Sun et al. introduce CO-Bench, a suite of 36 diverse combinatorial optimization problems (packing, scheduling, routing) designed specifically to benchmark LLM agents in generating algorithms (code), not just solutions. They evaluate 9 frameworks (including FunSearch, ReEvo, AIDE), finding that FunSearch combined with reasoning models (o3-mini) yields the most robust performance, though agents still struggle significantly with strict feasibility constraints (valid solution rates often <60%). **Takeaway:** We should immediately integrate CO-Bench into our pipeline to benchmark AlgoEvo against ReEvo and FunSearch; this saves us months of data curation and provides a standardized metric to prove our method's superiority.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Carnegie Mellon University

Generative AI for OR.title: ORLM: A Customizable Framework in Training Large Models for Automated Optimization Modeling
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Structured LLM-Driven Optimization Modeling via Verification and Self-Improving Agents
Generative AI for OR.brief: The authors propose OR-Instruct, a framework that uses GPT-4 to synthesize over 32k optimization modeling pairs (natural language to COPT code) to fine-tune 7B-scale models (ORLM). They demonstrate that these fine-tuned models outperform GPT-4 on their new 'IndustryOR' benchmark, a result that appears robust given the specialized nature of the task. The most valuable takeaway is their specific data augmentation strategy—iteratively altering constraints and injecting specific modeling techniques (e.g., Big M)—which provides a concrete recipe we can steal to generate diverse instances for our OR-Bench project. While the methodology is standard instruction tuning, the resulting artifacts (benchmark and model) establish a new baseline for automated OR modeling that we cannot ignore.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Columbia University, Duke University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, Shenzhen Research Institute of Big Data, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, Cardinal Operations

Generative AI for OR.title: Text2Zinc: A Cross-Domain Dataset for Modeling Optimization and Satisfaction Problems in MiniZinc
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Execution-Verified LLM Agents for OR Model and Algorithm Synthesis
Generative AI for OR.brief: Singirikonda et al. introduce TEXT2ZINC, a dataset of 110 Natural Language-to-MiniZinc problems, and benchmark GPT-4 using Vanilla, CoT, and Compositional prompting. Their results are poor (max ~25% solution accuracy), confirming that off-the-shelf LLMs struggle significantly with MiniZinc syntax and logical translation. Crucially, they attempt using Knowledge Graphs as an intermediate representation, but report that it actually *reduced* solution accuracy compared to basic CoT—a valuable negative result for our symbolic modeling work. We should examine their dataset for inclusion in OR-Bench, but their prompting methods are rudimentary baselines we should easily outperform.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Brown University, Fidelity Investments

Generative AI for OR.title: EquivaMap: Leveraging LLMs for Automatic Equivalence Checking of Optimization Formulations
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Execution-Verified LLM Agents for OR Model and Algorithm Synthesis
Generative AI for OR.brief: Zhai et al. propose EquivaMap, a framework that evaluates whether two MILP formulations are equivalent by using an LLM to discover a linear mapping between their decision variables, which is then rigorously verified by a solver. Unlike 'execution accuracy' (which fails on unit scaling) or 'canonical accuracy' (which fails on variable permutation), they achieve 100% accuracy on a new dataset of equivalent formulations including cuts and slack variables. The core insight is replacing output comparison with a 'propose-mapping-and-verify' loop, effectively using the LLM to construct a proof of equivalence. We must adopt this methodology for the OR-Bench evaluation pipeline immediately, as it eliminates the false negatives currently plaguing our generation benchmarks.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Stanford University, The University of Texas at Austin

Generative AI for OR.title: OptMATH: A Scalable Bidirectional Data Synthesis Framework for Optimization Modeling
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Structured LLM-Driven Optimization Modeling via Verification and Self-Improving Agents
Generative AI for OR.brief: The authors introduce OptMATH, a framework for generating synthetic optimization datasets by creating mathematical instances from seed generators, back-translating them to natural language via LLMs, and validating the pairs using a solver-based rejection sampling loop (checking if the re-generated model yields the same optimal value). They demonstrate that a Qwen-32B model fine-tuned on this data beats GPT-4 on NL4Opt and MAMO benchmarks. The critical takeaway is the **solver-verified reverse generation pipeline**: we should immediately steal this workflow to populate OR-Bench and generate diverse, verified training environments for AlgoEvo, replacing manual curation with scalable synthesis.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Peking University

Generative AI for OR.title: MoE2: Optimizing Collaborative Inference for Edge Large Language Models
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Structured LLM-Driven Optimization Modeling via Verification and Self-Improving Agents
Generative AI for OR.brief: Jin et al. introduce MoE2, a collaborative inference framework that uses discrete monotonic optimization to route queries to heterogeneous edge LLMs under latency and energy constraints. The results are backed by physical hardware experiments on NVIDIA Jetson and RTX 4090 devices, demonstrating up to 14.4% accuracy improvements on MMLU over single-agent baselines while respecting strict energy and delay budgets. The key insight is a theoretical proof showing that optimal gating parameters for a full set of LLM experts are preserved for any subset, allowing the decoupling of gating network training from the combinatorial expert selection process. While this is a competent application of operations research to LLM serving optimization, it is a lower priority read as it does not advance our primary focus on LLM evolutionary search or multi-agent optimization.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Zhejiang University, University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign Institute, Zhejiang Key Laboratory of Medical Imaging Artificial Intelligence

Generative AI for OR.title: BPP-Search: Enhancing Tree of Thought Reasoning for Mathematical Modeling Problem Solving
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Structured LLM-Driven Optimization Modeling via Verification and Self-Improving Agents
Generative AI for OR.brief: Wang et al. propose BPP-Search, combining Beam Search, a Process Reward Model (PRM), and a final Pairwise Preference Model to generate LP/MIP models from natural language. While their new 'StructuredOR' dataset is small (38 test instances), it uniquely provides intermediate modeling labels (sets, parameters, variables) essential for training PRMs in this domain. The key takeaway is their finding that PRMs are effective for pruning but imprecise for final ranking; they solve this by adding a pairwise preference model at the leaf layer—a technique we should immediately steal to improve selection robustness in our MASPRM and evolutionary search pipelines. This is a competent execution of 'LLM + Search' applied specifically to our OR niche.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Huawei, The University of Hong Kong

Generative AI for OR.title: Autoformulation of Mathematical Optimization Models Using LLMs
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Structured LLM-Driven Optimization Modeling via Verification and Self-Improving Agents
Generative AI for OR.brief: Astorga et al. frame optimization modeling as a hierarchical Monte-Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) problem, using LLMs to generate components and—crucially—employing SMT solvers to prune mathematically equivalent branches (e.g., recognizing `x+y` and `y+x` as identical). They achieve SOTA results on NL4OPT and IndustryOR, outperforming fine-tuned models like ORLM while using significantly fewer samples than naive approaches. **Key Takeaway:** The integration of symbolic equivalence checking (SMT) to prune the search tree is a technique we should immediately steal; implementing this in AlgoEvo would allow us to discard functionally identical code/math mutants before expensive evaluation, directly addressing our sample efficiency bottleneck.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: University of Cambridge, University of Hawaii at Manoa

Generative AI for OR.title: Generalists vs. Specialists: Evaluating LLMs on Highly-Constrained Biophysical Sequence Optimization Tasks
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Execution-Verified LLM Agents for OR Model and Algorithm Synthesis
Generative AI for OR.brief: The authors propose LLOME, a bilevel optimization framework that fine-tunes an LLM using 'MargE' (Margin-Aligned Expectation), a loss function that weights gradient updates by the magnitude of reward improvement (margin) rather than simple preference rankings. Results are rigorous and demonstrate that while DPO leads to generator collapse and infeasibility in constrained spaces, MargE maintains diversity and significantly improves sample efficiency, matching specialized solvers like LaMBO-2 on medium-difficulty tasks. The critical takeaway is that standard alignment methods (DPO/RLHF) are ill-suited for optimization because they discard information about *how much* better a solution is; MargE fixes this by satisfying the Strong Interpolation Criteria. We should immediately evaluate replacing the RL/update component in AlgoEvo with the MargE objective to improve the stability and quality of our evolved heuristics.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Genentech, New York University

Generative AI for OR.title: LLMOPT: Learning to Define and Solve General Optimization Problems from Scratch
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Structured LLM-Driven Optimization Modeling via Verification and Self-Improving Agents
Generative AI for OR.brief: The authors fine-tune Qwen1.5-14B to translate natural language optimization problems into Pyomo code via a structured 'five-element' intermediate representation (Sets, Parameters, Variables, Objective, Constraints) and KTO alignment. They achieve ~11% accuracy gains over GPT-4o and ORLM on benchmarks like NL4Opt and IndustryOR, primarily by reducing formulation hallucinations through the structured intermediate step and preference optimization. For our OR-Bench work, the key takeaway is the concrete recipe for using KTO to align symbolic modeling agents, which appears more effective than standard SFT for enforcing constraints in smaller models. While not an evolutionary search paper, it provides a strong, locally runnable baseline for our OR modeling evaluations.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Ant Group, East China Normal University, Nanjing University

Generative AI for OR.title: A Survey of Optimization Modeling Meets LLMs: Progress and Future Directions
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Structured LLM-Driven Optimization Modeling via Verification and Self-Improving Agents
Generative AI for OR.brief: This survey and empirical audit reveals that standard optimization modeling benchmarks (NL4Opt, IndustryOR) suffer from critical error rates ranging from 16% to 54%, rendering prior leaderboards unreliable. The authors manually cleaned these datasets and re-evaluated methods, finding that Chain-of-Thought (CoT) often degrades performance compared to standard prompting, while fine-tuned models (ORLM) and multi-agent systems (Chain-of-Experts) perform best. The immediate takeaway is that we must adopt their cleaned datasets for our OR-Bench project; using the original open-source versions is no longer defensible. Additionally, the failure of CoT on these tasks suggests we should prioritize multi-agent or fine-tuned approaches for symbolic formulation tasks.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Zhejiang University, Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab, Singapore University of Social Sciences, Hangzhou High-Tech Zone (Binjiang) Institute of Blockchain and Data Security

Generative AI for OR.title: OptiMUS-0.3: Using Large Language Models to Model and Solve Optimization Problems at Scale
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Advanced LLM Agents for Symbolic OR Modeling and Problem Reformulation
Generative AI for OR.brief: OptiMUS-0.3 is a modular multi-agent system that translates natural language into Gurobi code, utilizing a 'connection graph' to manage variable-constraint relationships in long contexts and specialized agents to detect solver-specific structures (SOS, indicators) or implement sifting. The results are rigorous, introducing a new hard benchmark (NLP4LP) where they outperform GPT-4o by ~40% and beat Chain-of-Experts. The most stealable insight is the 'Structure Detection Agent': instead of relying on the LLM to write generic constraints, we should explicitly prompt for and map high-level structures to efficient solver APIs (like SOS constraints) to improve performance in our EvoCut and AlgoEvo pipelines. This is a necessary read for the OR-Bench team.

Generative AI for OR.title: OptiBench Meets ReSocratic: Measure and Improve LLMs for Optimization Modeling
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Structured LLM-Driven Optimization Modeling via Verification and Self-Improving Agents
Generative AI for OR.brief: The authors propose OptiBench, a benchmark of 605 optimization problems (linear/nonlinear, tabular/text), and ReSocratic, a data synthesis method that generates formal models first and back-translates them into natural language questions. Results are strong: fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on their 29k synthetic samples improves accuracy from 13.6% to 51.1%, validating the data quality. **Key Takeaway:** The 'Reverse Socratic' synthesis pipeline (Formal Model → Code → NL Question) is the superior strategy for generating synthetic OR datasets because it guarantees solvability and ground truth by construction, unlike forward generation. We should steal this pipeline for generating robust test instances for OR-Bench and potentially for training our OR agents.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, ETH Zurich, Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab, City University of Hong Kong, Sun Yat-sen University, MBZUAI, University of California Merced, Chongqing University

Generative AI for OR.title: LLaMoCo: Instruction Tuning of Large Language Models for Optimization Code Generation
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Execution-Verified LLM Agents for OR Model and Algorithm Synthesis
Generative AI for OR.brief: LLaMoCo fine-tunes small LLMs (down to 350M) to generate executable Python optimization code by training on a synthetic dataset where the 'ground truth' is the empirically best-performing solver identified via exhaustive benchmarking. The results are compelling: the fine-tuned 350M model achieves ~85% normalized performance on benchmarks where GPT-4 Turbo only reaches ~14-30%, largely because the small model learns to select specialized evolutionary strategies (like BIPOP-CMA-ES) while GPT-4 defaults to generic gradient-based solvers. **Key Takeaway:** We can replace the expensive GPT-4 calls in our evolutionary search loop with a specialized, fine-tuned local model (CodeLlama-7B) trained on our historical search successes, significantly improving both sample efficiency and scalability. The paper's 'contrastive warm-up' strategy for aligning diverse problem descriptions is also a transferable technique for our problem encoding work.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Singapore Management University, Nanyang Technological University, South China University of Technology

Generative AI for OR.title: OptiMUS: Scalable Optimization Modeling with (MI)LP Solvers and Large Language Models
Generative AI for OR.front_name: Structured LLM-Driven Optimization Modeling via Verification and Self-Improving Agents
Generative AI for OR.brief: OptiMUS is a multi-agent framework for translating natural language into Gurobi code, achieving SOTA performance by using a 'Connection Graph' to map variables and parameters to specific constraints. This graph allows the agents to dynamically filter context and construct minimal prompts, enabling success on problems with long descriptions where baselines like Chain-of-Experts fail. They release NLP4LP, a hard benchmark of 67 complex instances, which we must immediately compare against our OR-Bench efforts. The **Connection Graph** is the key stealable insight: a structured dependency tracking mechanism that solves context pollution in iterative code generation, directly applicable to our AlgoEvo and HERMES memory designs.
Generative AI for OR.affiliations: Stanford University

OR for Generative AI.title: Scalable Placement for Disaggregated LLM Serving on Heterogeneous Edge Fleets
OR for Generative AI.brief: SPADE tackles placement of disaggregated prefill/decode LLM serving on heterogeneous edge fleets, using a congestion-aware fluid tandem queue objective, type-count candidate enumeration with dominance pruning, and closed-form water-filling layer partitioning solved via multidimensional knapsack DP/MILP. On 30-device synthetic fleets it finds verified optimum in 441 ms while GA+DP takes 6855s with 19.7% higher congestion, and pruning eliminates 99.6% of candidates without observed loss. The key insight is that device-type symmetry plus dominance can make exact replica selection tractable, and the water-filling closed form replaces expensive layer DP—worth adopting in LLM serving placement optimization. It matters because it turns previously heuristic search into exact, fast optimization for heterogeneous serving.
OR for Generative AI.affiliations: University of Oslo, UiT The Arctic University of Norway

OR for Generative AI.title: Optimal Scheduling of Multi-Site AI Data Centers in Day-Ahead Markets
OR for Generative AI.brief: Zhou and Cavraro present an LP that schedules GPU power caps, deferrable jobs, and online inference across three data-center sites to minimize day-ahead electricity cost, using 2025 CAISO prices and 210k GPUs. The 6.3% cost saving is decomposed into 3.8% price-independent efficiency, 2.3% temporal price response, and 0.2% spatial routing, backed by year-long simulation. The key transferable idea is the nested operating-mode decomposition, which prevents over-crediting power-cap efficiency as price-responsive flexibility—useful for any energy-aware scheduling evaluation. The piecewise-linear GPU throughput–power model is also a component worth incorporating into GPU scheduling formulations. It matters for energy-aware AI infrastructure scheduling, though it does not advance LLM evolutionary search.
OR for Generative AI.affiliations: National Laboratory of the Rockies

OR for Generative AI.title: eFAIR: Fair LLM Serving under Hourly Electricity Commitments
OR for Generative AI.brief: eFAIR is an online LLM serving scheduler that coordinates request dispatching, electricity budget allocation, and GPU frequency selection to maximize leximin-fair normalized request throughput under an hourly electricity commitment. Results on H20 and H200 configurations with 32 replicas show 28.0%-31.0% higher tenth-percentile normalized throughput than the best budget-feasible baseline, with absolute commitment deviation below 0.26%. The key insight is using a common normalized-throughput target to align request priority, future electricity reservations, and frequency choices, with surplus electricity used to accelerate higher-entitlement requests. This matters for energy-constrained LLM serving and GPU resource-allocation research, though it has little relevance to LLM evolutionary search.
OR for Generative AI.affiliations: HKUST

OR for Generative AI.title: Coordinating Distributed AI Servers with Industrial Loads to Reduce Grid-Interconnection Needs
OR for Generative AI.brief: Lyu and Xu formulate a joint MILP for sizing CPU/GPU server groups, scheduling deadline-constrained firm/flexible AI tasks, and routing tasks across factories to minimize annualized server, interconnection, and energy costs. Using 2030 demand projections and measured hourly production loads for 31 Chinese manufacturing industries, they report that factory-site deployment reduces additional grid-interconnection capacity by 60–63% versus new data centers, and by 98% with cross-site routing, from 1,488 MW to 30 MW nationally. Results are backed by public code and real load data, though the analysis is deterministic and routing benefits are an unconstrained upper bound. The key transferable insight is that co-locating AI workloads with existing heterogeneous loads and exploiting non-coincident peak capacity can substantially reduce infrastructure requirements. This is relevant to OR for AI infrastructure, but its contribution is an application-specific MILP case study rather than a methodological advance for LLM serving or GPU scheduling.
OR for Generative AI.affiliations: Columbia University

OR for Generative AI.title: Reducing Batch Makespan for LLM Agent Workloads through Inference-Environment Coordination
OR for Generative AI.brief: Feng et al. propose coordinated inference-environment optimizations for batch execution of multi-turn LLM agent tasks, including a workload-aware hybrid-cache allocation model, trajectory-label-based routing/scheduling, and capacity separation with Chain-Advancing Action Scheduling. Live experiments with Ling-3.0/3.1-Flash on BFCL, SWE-bench Multilingual, WideSearch, and MCP-Atlas report 10.4–65.0% makespan reductions with aligned scores, and controlled replay isolates individual optimizations. The key insight is that separating sample admission from environment execution and scheduling pending environment jobs by observed chain progress can substantially improve GPU utilization and shorten batch tails under constrained tool capacity. The workload-aware cache model also provides a simple way to choose cache ratio and concurrency for hybrid LLMs. This is useful for LLM serving scheduling but is not central to LLM evolutionary search methods.
OR for Generative AI.affiliations: Ant Group

OR for Generative AI.title: Spot Markets for AI Inference: Dynamic Capacity Allocation and Pricing on a Shared Accelerator Fleet
OR for Generative AI.brief: The paper formulates dynamic spot pricing and placement for a shared LLM inference fleet as a model-predictive-control problem solved by a small LP, deriving a batching-induced latency exchange rate, optimal slack pricing, backfill reliability, and placement hysteresis. Numerical results are backed by paired simulations with 20 random draws and standard errors, showing a 7.4% profit gain over fixed half-price practice and capturing 93% of the perfect-forecast gain on a stylized 512-accelerator week. The key insight is that continuous batching turns interactive-vs-spot capacity into a linear displacement constraint, with one interactive token per second displacing rho_m > 1 spot tokens per second, making pricing and placement tractable through shadow prices. This is relevant to LLM serving scheduling and resource allocation because it provides a principled cost/price model for latency tiers, deadlines, and power caps, though it does not address LLM evolutionary search or multi-agent coordination.
OR for Generative AI.affiliations: New York University

OR for Generative AI.title: Asymptotic Optimality of $cμ$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint
OR for Generative AI.brief: Li et al. develop a fluid-limit queueing model for LLM inference scheduling under KV-cache memory constraints and prove that a cμ priority rule with effective service rates minimizes holding cost and completion time; they also introduce a smoothed cμ-inspired policy for finite systems. On an NVIDIA H800 with production traces, cμ-backfill reduces average latency from 35.5s to 9.5s on To-B and from 30.2s to 10.4s on semi-synthetic workloads compared with vLLM, while remaining competitive with or better than SVF/MC-SF/WAIT. The key transferable idea is to compute effective service rates from prefill compute, KV-cache I/O, and memory capacity, then use cμ ordering plus future-KV feasibility checks for admission and backfilling. This is a relevant, theory-backed scheduling method for LLM serving under memory constraints; it does not change LLM evolutionary search approaches.
OR for Generative AI.affiliations: HKUST, University of Southern California

OR for Generative AI.title: Layer-wise CPU-GPU Scheduling for LLM Inference on Memory-Limited Consumer GPUs
OR for Generative AI.brief: This paper presents a layer-wise CPU/GPU placement and scheduling method for LLM inference on memory-limited single-GPU systems. It models decode latency as max(total computation, total transfer) after relaxing transfer timing constraints and uses a continued-fraction search to choose the ratio of CPU-executed layers to GPU streamed layers. On a consumer RTX 5090, it reports 3.5x speedup over HuggingFace Accelerate and 6.3x over DeepSpeed ZeRO-Inference for OPT-30B, hiding 99.6% of transfers; however, it is 22% slower than SplitGen for Llama2-70B under host-memory pressure. The key insight is that CPU computation during batch-size-1 decode can be deliberately used as a planned window to hide weight transfers, with simple average-based ratio balancing providing strong offloading gains. This is relevant to LLM serving scheduling, but it is not a fundamental advance and lacks code release and statistical rigor.
OR for Generative AI.affiliations: Keio University, SoftBank Corp.

OR for Generative AI.title: Queuing for Inference: Dynamic Memory Footprints and Costly Preemption
OR for Generative AI.brief: This paper introduces a queueing model for LLM inference serving that couples attained-service-dependent KV-cache growth, finite memory capacity with service slowdown, and memory-proportional preemption overhead. It shows that classical Gittins scheduling can become unstable under costly preemption and proposes MLPT, a multi-level age-threshold policy with derived mean response time and an empirical rule for threshold selection. Simulations over 100,000 jobs show 15–50% mean response time reductions over FCFS and stable behavior where capped Gittins degrades. The key insight is that optimal scheduling balances short-job priority against memory-dependent preemption overhead, with the memory slowdown threshold serving as a natural preemption point in limited-memory regimes. This is relevant for LLM serving scheduling theory but remains an analytical/simulation study without real-system validation.
OR for Generative AI.affiliations: Purdue University

OR for Generative AI.title: Efficient KV Cache Migration for Geo-Distributed LLM Inference in Collaborative Edge Computing
OR for Generative AI.brief: Zhang et al. propose EdgeFlow, a hybrid KV cache migration scheme for geo-distributed collaborative edge LLM inference that combines direct KV cache transmission with activation-based recomputation, overlapped in a pipeline. They formulate a multi-node migration problem and give a 2-approximation algorithm based on LP relaxation and bipartite perfect matching. Experiments on a real 100+ GPU testbed with Qwen2.5-32B and Llama3.1-70B report up to 45.8% migration time reduction over direct transmission, though statistical rigor is limited. The key transferable idea is treating KV cache migration as a scheduling problem where choosing between data movement and recomputation adapts to heterogeneous bandwidth and compute, a perspective useful for LLM serving scheduling. This matters for OR/optimization methods applied to LLM inference infrastructure, but it is not a breakthrough for the team's primary evolutionary search agenda.
OR for Generative AI.affiliations: The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, National University of Defense Technology, Wuhan University

OR for Generative AI.title: Vesta: Queueing-Aware LLM Scheduling for Real-World Workloads
OR for Generative AI.brief: Zou et al. present Vesta, a queueing-aware scheduler for distributed agentic LLM serving that separates stable hashed KV-cache holders from per-request executors and prices the queueing externality of each placement via an M/M/c-derived congestion function. On production agentic traces, Vesta improves throughput by 14.0% and reduces mean TTFT by 57.8% over SMetric in PD-colocated deployments, and reduces mean/P99 TTFT by up to 18.1%/29.0% in disaggregated settings; these gains are backed by real trace replays on 32-instance clusters. The key transferable idea is to charge only the incremental service demand beyond the cheapest candidate using a utilization- and Erlang-waiting-probability-based price, which automatically favors migration under slack and locality under congestion. This is directly useful for OR-based LLM serving scheduling and should be considered when formulating cluster-scheduling objectives, though the paper lacks released code and repeated-run variance.
OR for Generative AI.affiliations: Tencent, The Chinese University of Hong Kong

OR for Generative AI.title: Dissecting the Carbon-SLO Tension in Geo-Distributed LLM Serving
OR for Generative AI.brief: Topcu et al. build a hardware-calibrated geo-distributed LLM serving simulator that models continuous batching, queueing, and per-phase power, and evaluate four carbon-aware schedulers including a facility MILP that prices batched energy collectively. Results report 26–60% carbon savings over round-robin with about 3% average SLO violations, with savings growing with carbon-intensity spread and shrinking under high load; the numbers are backed by calibrated latency/power models and end-to-end validation. The key useful idea is to use engine-level active batch load and queue depth to estimate TTFT/TPOT at scheduling time, and to charge per-datacenter fixed energy as a facility cost in a MILP, which gives a strong carbon–SLO balance. This is relevant for LLM serving scheduling and batch resource allocation, though it is not a fundamental advance for LLM evolutionary search or multi-agent optimization.
OR for Generative AI.affiliations: Pennsylvania State University

OR for Generative AI.title: TokenRouter: Efficient Serving System for Token-Level LLM Routing
OR for Generative AI.brief: TokenRouter presents a serving system for token-level LLM routing, using request-centric programming and model-centric subservers with asynchronous tri-loop execution, a handoff-resume KV-cache mechanism, and a delayed-batching scheduler whose threshold is derived from a DTMC throughput model. The paper reports 2.01–64.15× throughput gains over official and SGLang-based baselines across five routing algorithms and multiple workloads, with ablation breakdowns showing delayed batching contributes materially. The key insight is that controlled batching delay, optimized via a formal Markov-chain throughput model, can substantially reduce batch admission delay for irregular multi-model token arrivals; the handoff-resume pending state also avoids costly prefix rematching. This is relevant for LLM serving scheduling, providing a concrete queueing/scheduling design that could inform batch scheduling for multi-model inference, though it is outside LLM evolutionary search.
OR for Generative AI.affiliations: Tsinghua University, Carnegie Mellon University

OR for Generative AI.title: JOVE: Joint Execution and Verification for Resource-Aware LLM Task Graphs
OR for Generative AI.brief: Zhang et al. propose an online MILP framework that jointly assigns executor LLMs to task-graph nodes and chooses which node outputs to pay to verify, under a long-term average API-cost budget and per-query latency chance constraints. On four reasoning benchmarks, JOVE reports accuracy comparable to unconstrained baselines while using 3.7–16.3x lower cost and 8.3–17.0x lower latency, though results are mean ± std over only three random orderings with no significance tests. The key transferable idea is the D-optimal information-gain bonus that makes verification a decision variable: a node is verified when the expected reduction in parameter uncertainty exceeds its priced verification cost, enabling selective paid feedback to improve future allocations. This matters for resource-constrained LLM serving, task-graph orchestration, and active selection of process reward labels in multi-agent optimization.
OR for Generative AI.affiliations: University of Texas at Austin, DEVCOM Army Research Laboratory

OR for Generative AI.title: Predictive Rolling-Horizon Optimization for Commitment-Aware Model-Parallel Inference under Spatio-Temporal Edge Dynamics
OR for Generative AI.brief: Liwang et al. propose PROMISE, a predictive rolling-horizon framework that jointly schedules model-parallel DNN inference tasks and sets committed completion times under stochastic arrivals and load-dependent edge capacity. Simulations over 400 timeslots and a Raspberry Pi cluster show improved task completion and reward relative to several baselines, though quantitative gaps are only shown in figures without variance or significance tests. The key transferable idea is treating service commitments as endogenous decisions and recovering CCTs analytically from rollout-predicted completion times, with a progress-aware surrogate for evaluating current mappings.
